# Intake brief — Hex Map Information UX (AH-0MWL4QCVD007WOAM)

## Headline

The Hex Map screen (`HexMapScene`) draws roughly fifteen separately positioned
text objects and a ring of tiles with **no sectioning at all**: war status,
transient "what just happened" news, the map itself, the selected hex's intel and
the controls legend all float over the same background, in three different
columns and two different font conventions. This item introduces named,
visually bounded **sections** — each with its own heading — so every group of
information is distinguishable at a glance.

## Problem statement

There is a lot of information on the Hex Map and too little structure holding it
apart. Measured against the shipped renderer (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts`,
960×540), the screen currently carries:

| What is drawn | Where it sits today |
|---|---|
| Screen title, and the run result line (`RUN: VICTORY · score N`) | centred, top (`y=18`, `y=46`) |
| Ring progress (`RING 2 — 3/12 HEXES HELD`) | left column (`x=24`, `y=62`) |
| Frontier strength (`FRONTIER · STR n · BEAT ≤ m (k IN REACH)`) | left column (`y=82`) |
| Hangar fleet + bank (`HANGAR · hull · n min · n cores`) | left column (`y=102`) |
| `ATTACK — FOCUSED HEX` panel (rolled-in defence report) | left column (`y=118`, conditional) |
| `HANGAR ASSAULT` banner (ring won / hangar falls) | left column (`y=300`, conditional) |
| `◀ HANGAR` action row | left column (`y=468`) |
| `READ THE MAP` legend, six lines of static help | right column (`y=112`–`y=182`) |
| `SELECTED HEX — FULL INTEL` detail panel | right column (`y=200`) |
| Hex tiles (`AGG n` + ownership marker + `(q,r)`), attack arrows, hangar marker | centre |
| Keyboard hint line | bottom centre (`y=530`) |

Three problems follow from that inventory:

1. **Unlike information is adjacent, like information is apart.** The three
   left-hand header lines mix ring progress, frontier combat maths and hangar
   inventory with no heading to separate them, while the two halves of "the
   selected hex" (its intel, right column; its attack row, left column) sit on
   opposite sides of the screen.
2. **Transient news has no home.** The run result is centred at the top, the
   hangar-assault outcome is a left-hand banner, and the banked win-bonus line
   (`model.winBonusLine`) is computed but **never drawn at all** — its only
   consumer is the `getWinBonusLine()` test seam. "What just happened" therefore
   arrives in up to three different places, one of which is nowhere.
3. **Help competes with content.** A six-line static legend occupies the top of
   the same right-hand column as the dynamic intel panel it explains, so the
   loudest text in that column is documentation rather than information about
   the player's war.

## Users

- **The Hangar War player** landing on the map between sorties.
  - *As a player, I want the map's status, my last sortie's outcome, the ring
    itself and the selected hex's intel each in their own labelled section, so I
    can find one thing without reading everything.*
  - *As a player, I want to know what just happened (victory/defeat, ring won or
    hangar falls, minerals banked) in one place, so I do not have to hunt three
    corners of the screen for the aftermath of my deployment.*
  - *As a player reading the selected hex, I want its intel and its attack row
    together, so one hex is one story rather than two panels apart.*
  - *As a colour-blind player, I want sections distinguished by headings and
    framing rather than by colour alone, consistent with the map's existing
    CVD-safe conventions.*
- **The maintainer** of the shared `buildHexMapModel` → `renderHexMap` pair,
  who needs the section layout to live in one renderer so the game and the
  `GymHexWar` parity gym cannot drift (AGENTS.md gym↔game parity).

## Producer decisions (2026-11-17)

- **Q1 = (a)** — sections are **bordered, headed panels** laid out in fixed
  columns; every section has a frame, a heading and a bounded rect.
- **Q2 = (b)** — **four content sections plus a controls footer**: WAR STATUS,
  LAST SORTIE, MAP, SELECTED HEX (intel **and** its attack row together), and
  CONTROLS/LEGEND.
- **Q3 = (a)** — the banked win-bonus line **is rendered**, inside LAST SORTIE.

## Section model (producer-approved)

Four content sections plus a controls footer, each drawn as a **bordered,
headed panel** with a bounded rect:

| Section | Contains | Visibility |
|---|---|---|
| `war-status` | ring progress, frontier strength / beatable ceiling / in-reach count, hangar hull + banked minerals/cores | always |
| `last-sortie` | run result line, banked win bonus, hangar-assault outcome (`RING WON…` / `HANGAR FALLS…`) | only when the landing carries one of those |
| `map` | the ring tiles, attack arrows and hangar marker | always |
| `selected-hex` | the focused hex's full intel **and** its `ATTACK — FOCUSED HEX` row | always (panel body may be empty when nothing is focused) |
| `controls` | keyboard hint line + the `READ THE MAP` legend | always |

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Section registry on the shared view.** `HexMapView` publishes a `sections`
  list — `{ key, heading, rect }` per rendered section — and every rendered text
  object, tile and arrow lies inside **exactly one** section rect, with no two
  section rects overlapping and every rect inside the 960×540 frame.
- **Every section is a bordered, headed panel (Q1 = a).** Each of `war-status`,
  `last-sortie` (when shown), `map`, `selected-hex` and `controls` draws a panel
  frame and one heading from a shared exported constant (`WAR STATUS`,
  `LAST SORTIE`, `SELECTED HEX`, `CONTROLS`, and the map's own title), in one
  consistent style and position convention, so the groupings are distinguishable
  without relying on colour.
- **No information is lost.** Every string the current renderer draws still
  renders, in its new section; the tile labels (`AGG n`, ownership marker,
  `(q,r)`), arrows, hint line and legend text are unchanged in content.
- **Transient news is grouped and complete (Q2 = b, Q3 = a).** The run result
  line, the hangar-assault banner and the banked win-bonus line
  (`WIN BONUS BANKED: +N MINERALS`, from `model.winBonusLine`) render **only**
  inside `last-sortie`; the win-bonus line is now actually drawn, not merely
  queryable. When the landing carries none of the three, the section is absent
  (no empty headed box).
- **One hex, one section.** The selected hex's intel and its attack row render
  inside the same `selected-hex` section; the attack row is hidden (not moved to
  another section) when the focused hex is in no attack.
- **Help no longer competes with content.** The `READ THE MAP` legend moves into
  the `controls` section and no longer occupies the intel column.
- **Legibility at 960×540.** No section body text overdraws a hex tile or the
  hangar marker; long strings (draw name, assault arithmetic) word-wrap inside
  their section; no rendered text is smaller than today's smallest (9px) and
  headings are at least 10px.
- **Game/gym parity, one shared layout.** All layout lives in
  `renderHexMap`/`hexMap.ts`; `GymHexWar` renders the same sections read-only
  through the same call, and no gym-local or scene-local layout exists (the
  existing `renderHexMap` equivalence assertions stay green).
- **Interaction contract unchanged.** Grid arrow navigation, Tab/Shift+Tab
  cycling, Enter/Space inspect-or-deploy, tile hover/click, the `◀ HANGAR` row
  and ESC-to-menu behave exactly as before; the attract traversal still takes
  exactly one next action and cannot stall on a section.
- **Regression coverage.** `HexMapScene.test.ts`, the renderer/`hexIntel` tests
  and `GymHexWar.test.ts` pin the section registry (keys, headings, non-overlap,
  in-frame), `last-sortie` visibility toggling, and that the selected-hex intel
  and attack row share a section; position-only pins may be updated, behaviour
  pins may not be weakened.
- **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries** — GDD §8.2 (the
  map's screen surface), the `hexMap.ts` module docblock, and
  `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` if its row description changes.
- **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Impact

A Hangar War player can read the map at a glance: the war's status, the last
sortie's outcome, the ring itself, the selected hex's intel and the controls each
sit in their own labelled section instead of scattering across three columns.

## Constraints

- **Renderer-only change.** The model (`src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts`) stays
  the single source of every string; `hexMap.ts` only draws and positions. No
  gameplay rule, resolver call or persisted state is added.
- **One layout for game and gym.** The gym↔game parity contract and the existing
  `renderHexMap` equivalence assertions forbid a second layout implementation.
- **Single 960×540 viewport.** No scrolling, panning, tabs or collapsible
  sections unless the producer chooses the tabbed option in Q1.
- **Transient launch data stays transient** — run result, tick record, assault
  and win bonus are never persisted; a later entry renders no `last-sortie`.
- **Existing CVD-safe conventions hold** — section distinction must not depend on
  colour; the tile ownership encoding (blue/orange + filled/hollow marker) is
  untouched.
- **No new assets or fonts** — monospace text and Phaser Graphics panels only.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts` (951 lines) holds every layout constant
  (`PANEL_X`, `ATTACK_PANEL_Y`, `ASSAULT_BANNER_Y`, legend rows, hint line) and
  draws all of the inventory above. There is no section abstraction: each text
  object is positioned by a hand-tuned literal.
- `HexMapView` already exposes behavioural seams (`getRows`, `getArrows`,
  `getPanelText`, `getLeftPanelText`, `getAssaultText`, …) but nothing describing
  screen regions, so no test can currently assert grouping or non-overlap.
- `model.winBonusLine` exists (`src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts` →
  `defenceReport.ts`) and is surfaced only by `HexMapScene.getWinBonusLine()`;
  the renderer never draws it.
- Prior work already fixed the map's *readability* (reveal filter, CVD-safe tiles,
  coordinates, titled detail-panel lines) and its *navigation* (grid arrows), so
  this item is the remaining structural/visual-hierarchy step.

## Desired change

A sectioned Hex Map: a small number of named, bounded regions with headings, each
holding one kind of information, drawn by the shared renderer so the game and the
parity gym stay identical; transient sortie news gathered into one place; the
selected hex's intel and attack row brought together; help demoted to a controls
footer.

## Key Files

**Key Files:**

- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts` — the whole layout: section rects, headings,
  legend relocation, last-sortie grouping; add `sections` to `HexMapView`
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts` — shared section-heading constants and any
  model wiring for the last-sortie lines (`winBonusLine` is already published)
- `src/scenes/HexMapScene.ts` — query seam for `sections`, transient launch data
  plumbing (no rule change)
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.ts` — renders the same sections read-only
- `src/scenes/HexMapScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.test.ts`,
  `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.test.ts` — section/grouping pins; update
  position-only assertions
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §8.2 and `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` — describe the
  sectioned map surface

## Related work

- **AH-0MVUXCAG90086LH2** — Hex map scene with known-ahead intel (completed): the
  scene and its intel model this item re-lays-out.
- **AH-0MWDBI33V003QQ3U** — Hangar Map UX (completed, parent): reveal filter,
  CVD-safe ownership, coordinates on tiles, spatial arrows — the readability and
  navigation pass that precedes this structural one.
- **AH-0MWJ0XHWW009GTKK** — Hangar Map UI: clearer overview (completed): titled
  every line of the selected-hex intel. Its line titles are load-bearing for
  this item's `selected-hex` section and must not be disturbed.
- **AH-0MWEWYUAS002P7P9** — Renderer: CVD-safe labels, reveal filter, owned-hex
  selection (completed); **AH-0MWEWYVD7008PPQT** — Navigation: grid columns
  (completed): both pin renderer behaviour this item must preserve.
- **AH-0MWDC3L9I008INDP** — Defence report rolled into the hex map (completed):
  source of the attack arrows and the left-hand attack panel now moved into
  `selected-hex`.
- **AH-0MWEZZA4E0081NJ5** — Assault defence report and reset announcement
  (completed): source of the `HANGAR ASSAULT` banner now grouped under
  `last-sortie`.
- **AH-0MWF0CWB7002MG2F** — Special-mission intel (completed): the `★ SPECIAL`
  tile tag whose detail-panel block lives in `selected-hex`.
- **AH-0MWEVNBMM000QFO2** — Win path: bank a fixed post-win bonus (open): owns the
  `winBonusLine` whose presentation Q3 decides.
- **AH-0MW3VG6WJ004HRI9** — Text on hex map is unreadable (completed): the
  legibility baseline this item must not regress.

### Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MVUXCAG90086LH2** – Hex map scene with known-ahead intel (completed)
- **AH-0MTGBPRYC000QIHU** – Player has no audio (completed)
- **AH-0MW3VG6WJ004HRI9** – Text on hex map is unreadable (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: clearly, create, easily, group, hex, hexmap, identify, information, logical, lot, make, map, much, page, presented, sections, sense, there
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: clearly, create, distinguishable, group, hex, hexmap, lot, make, map, much, page, sections, there
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — matched: create, group, hex, hexmap, logical, lot, make, map, much, page, presented, there

Keyword false positive: `AH-0MTGBPRYC000QIHU` (audio) matched on generic words
(`make`, `there`) and is not related to this item.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Clutter inversion.** More framing can add more visual noise than it removes;
  mitigation: a small fixed section count (4 + footer by default), one heading
  style, and the non-overlap/fit assertions as the guard.
- **Text reflow collisions.** Wrapped draw names and long assault arithmetic are
  the strings that collide at 960×540; mitigation: wrap widths inside each
  section rect plus the "no body text overdraws a tile" assertion.
- **Parity drift.** A scene-local tweak would break gym↔game parity; mitigation:
  all layout in `hexMap.ts`, with the existing equivalence assertions kept.
- **Test churn on positions.** Several suites assert coordinates indirectly;
  mitigation: pin sections structurally (`sections` registry) rather than by
  literal pixel offsets, and update only position-only assertions.
- **Scope creep** into a full visual redesign, new fonts, or tabbed navigation;
  such opportunities are recorded as new linked work items, not absorbed here.
- **Assumption:** headings are monospace text in the existing style (no new
  assets); **assumption:** the attract/demo traversal gains no new state, because
  every section is read-only like today's panels.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (ANSWERED, producer chose (a)) — How should the sections be delineated?**
  (a) Bordered, headed panels in fixed columns — every section has a frame, a
  heading and a bounded rect (recommended).
  (b) Headed bands with separator rules only — headings plus horizontal rules,
  no boxes, more breathing space over the map background.
  (c) Collapsible/tabbed sections — only one section expanded at a time, cutting
  on-screen text but adding interaction state and hidden information.
  **Recommended:** (a) — a frame per section is the most unambiguous
  distinction, needs no new interaction, and is directly assertable (rect +
  heading + non-overlap) by the existing scene/renderer tests.
  — **Answer (producer, 2026-11-17): (a)** bordered, headed panels in fixed
  columns. Source: interactive reply to the intake questions.

- **Q2 (ANSWERED, producer chose (b)) — Which grouping taxonomy should the map use?**
  (a) Six sections: WAR STATUS, LAST SORTIE, MAP, SELECTED HEX, ATTACK,
  CONTROLS/LEGEND.
  (b) Four sections plus a footer: WAR STATUS, LAST SORTIE, MAP, SELECTED HEX
  (intel **and** its attack row together), CONTROLS/LEGEND (recommended).
  (c) Keep today's regions and only add headings/separators to each.
  **Recommended:** (b) — it separates the three genuinely unlike kinds of
  information (war state, transient news, focused-hex detail) while keeping one
  hex's intel and attack row together, and it avoids the extra section that
  option (a) spends on material that is about the same focused hex.
  Research: the inventory in *Problem statement* comes from
  `src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts`; the attack panel and the detail panel are both
  keyed by the focused hex (`model.attackDetails` / `displayedHexKey`), which is
  what makes (b) coherent.
  — **Answer (producer, 2026-11-17): (b)** four sections plus a controls footer,
  with the focused hex's intel and its attack row in one `selected-hex` section.
  Source: interactive reply to the intake questions.

- **Q3 (ANSWERED, producer chose (a)) — Should the banked win-bonus line be
  rendered as part of this item?**
  (a) Yes — render `model.winBonusLine` (`WIN BONUS BANKED: +N MINERALS`) inside
  LAST SORTIE (recommended).
  (b) No — leave it query-only and record it as deliberately out of scope.
  (c) Remove the unused line/model field entirely.
  **Recommended:** (a) — the line already exists and is tested through the query
  seam; without it the "what just happened" section silently omits a reward the
  player just earned, and it is a one-line addition to a section this item is
  already building.
  Research: `winBonusLine` is produced by `defenceReport.ts` and republished by
  `hexIntel.ts`; `hexMap.ts` never draws it and `HexMapScene.getWinBonusLine()`
  is its only reader.
  — **Answer (producer, 2026-11-17): (a)** render `model.winBonusLine` inside
  `last-sortie`. Source: interactive reply to the intake questions.

- **Q4 (recorded, not blocking) — Is a repo/gym search needed for the selected-hex
  line titles?** Answered by inspection of AH-0MWJ0XHWW009GTKK: the titles
  (`ID:`, `STATE:`, `BOSS:`, `STRENGTHS:`, …) are shipped and are treated as a
  fixed input here. Source: work item description + `hexIntel.ts` constants.

# Completing a hex battle means the equipped hulls/weapons/plugins are reset

## Problem statement

The hangar currently treats the **whole fleet as permanent**: a deployed ship is not consumed when a battle ends, and buying an upgrade does not arm it. The producer wants each deployed ship to be a **one-battle consumable** — the flown hull, its equipped starting weapons and modifiers, and their bought permanent levels are spent on **win or loss** — while owned items the player did not fly, and the free starter kit, survive. Re-fitting a new ship must be quick, so **buying an upgrade should enable it immediately**, and a follow-on item will add saved ship configurations for one-action re-purchase.

## Users

- **Primary — the player** building and flying ships through the hex war.
- **Secondary — the balance/progression owner**, because the salvage economy must now fund re-fitting after every sortie.

Example user stories:

- As a player, after a battle I want the ship I flew to be spent, so each sortie is a real commitment and losing one costs me the ship, not my whole collection.
- As a player, I want buying an upgrade to arm it immediately, so re-fitting a new ship takes one action per part instead of buy-then-hunt-for-equip.
- As a player, I want the owned items I did not fly to survive, so a bad run never erases my progress.
- As a player, I want to keep the free starter hull and starter weapon, so I can always deploy after a wipe.

## Acceptance Criteria

- On completion of a hex deployment — **win or loss** — the deployed ship is removed from the hangar payload: the deployed hull (unless it is the free starter hull), every starting weapon in the hangar's active loadout (unless it is the free starter weapon), every modifier in that loadout, and the `weaponLevels` / `powerUpLevels` rows for those consumed ids are deleted. Every owned item the player did not deploy, and the free starter kit, remain owned.
- After the consumption the hangar is reset to the free starter kit: `activeHull` is the starter hull and `activeLoadout` is empty, so the next deployment uses only the free starter kit until the player re-purchases. The player's `bankedMinerals` and `bankedCores` are unchanged by consumption (the existing win bonus still applies on a win).
- A successful hangar purchase **auto-enables** the entry: a hull sets `activeHull`, a starting weapon joins `activeLoadout.startingWeapons`, and a modifier joins `activeLoadout.modifiers`; a refused purchase (`owned` / `gated` / `unaffordable`) changes neither ownership nor the loadout. This deliberately supersedes the economy's current "buying never equips" rule for the hangar screen, while other callers can keep the old behaviour through an explicit option.
- Automated tests cover both outcome paths and the purchase paths through the pure core and the scene seam (gym↔game parity): win and loss consumption, starter-kit survival, un-flown owned items surviving, consumed items' level rows removed, no soft-lock with an empty loadout, demo mode not overwriting the player's war, and auto-enable plus refusal for hull/weapon/modifier.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

After every hex battle the ship you flew is spent and you rebuild from the salvage you earned — and because buying an upgrade now arms it immediately, re-fitting a new ship takes fewer steps and each sortie feels like a real commitment.

## Constraints

- **No soft-lock.** The free starter hull (`hull-1`) and starter weapon (`spread`) are always owned; an empty loadout is legal (deploy with the ship's permanent cannon only, AH-0MVZJ6V1J001DA9D).
- **One payload write per battle** through the existing `saveHangarWarPayload`; defensive parsing stays the authority; no schema-version bump expected because the shape is unchanged.
- **Demo/attract runs never overwrite the player's war** — the existing `_saveHangarWarPayload` demo guard must keep holding for the consumed payload.
- **Gym↔game parity.** The consumption rule lives in the pure core and is exercised by the headless harness; no scene-only logic.
- **Supersedes a prior decision.** `hangarEconomy.buy()` currently documents that "buying only grants ownership — equipping stays the deployment selector's job" (A5/A6). This item overrides that for the hangar screen only.
- **Separate concern left alone.** The ring-end hangar-falls reset (`resetCampaign`, AH-0MWEZZ9TE001577J) already wipes both axes and is unchanged.
- **No new balance tuning.** The existing win bonus (`bankWinBonus` / `WIN_BONUS_MINERALS`) already provides the "wins pay more" difference the producer described.

## Existing state

- `buy()` in `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts` spends the price and adds the entry to the owned set, but deliberately does **not** equip it.
- `resolveHexCapture` and `resolveDeploymentDefeat` in `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts` clone the payload and currently **preserve** `hangar.activeHull` and `hangar.activeLoadout`.
- `HangarWarDeployment` (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.ts`) already carries the deployed `hullId`, `startingWeapons`, `modifiers` and the carried war `payload`, so the scene has the ship identity at battle end.
- `parseHangar` (`src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts`) restores `activeHull` / `activeLoadout`; `createDefaultPayload` seeds the starter hull and starter weapon as owned, not equipped.
- Permanent levels live in `hangar.weaponLevels` / `hangar.powerUpLevels`.
- Precedent: `resolveHexCapture` already derives the hex's defending bot from the deployed hull (`leaveDefender`), so "the flown hull is spent" fits the existing capture model.

## Desired change

- Add a **pure consumption reducer** (for example `consumeDeployedShip(hangar, ship, catalogue)`) that removes the flown hull, equipped starting weapons and modifiers plus their level rows, resets `activeHull` to the starter hull and clears `activeLoadout`, and preserves the starter kit and every un-flown owned item.
- Apply it on **both** the win path (`resolveHexCapture`) and the loss path (`resolveDeploymentDefeat`), driven by the deployment's hull and the hangar's active loadout.
- Add **auto-enable on purchase** to the hangar purchase path (`purchaseHangarEntry` / `buy` with an explicit `equipOnPurchase` option), keeping `buy`'s default non-equipping behaviour for other callers.
- Update the hangar screen so a purchase reads as equipped immediately, and update the affected unit/integration tests and docs.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts` — add the pure `consumeDeployedShip` reducer and an `equipOnPurchase` option on `buy`; keep the default non-equipping for other callers.
- `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts` — consume on the `resolveHexCapture` win path and the `resolveDeploymentDefeat` loss path; thread the deployed ship into both.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.ts` — expose the exact equipped set (hull + active loadout) that consumption applies to.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — pass the deployment's hull/loadout into the capture and defeat resolvers.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts` — `purchaseHangarEntry` uses `equipOnPurchase` and renders the auto-equipped state immediately.
- `src/scenes/HangarScene.ts` — persist the auto-equipped purchase through the same payload write.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts` — confirm the consumed/auto-equipped payload round-trips; no schema bump expected.
- Tests beside each module plus the `hangarWarFlow` integration test.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Economy treadmill.** Consuming the flown ship every battle could feel punitive, especially after a loss. Mitigation: wins pay more salvage (existing bonus), and the saved-configuration follow-on (AH-0MWL8C6FE008G1E7) makes re-fitting one action; validate against the ring-timing budgets before advancing.
- **Soft-lock.** Consumption must never remove the starter kit or leave no deployable ship. Mitigation: always retain `hull-1` and `spread`, and keep the empty-loadout rule (AH-0MVZJ6V1J001DA9D); test it.
- **Silent loss of un-flown levels.** Removing level rows must target only the deployed ids. Mitigation: consume the resolved deployed ids only, and assert un-flown `weaponLevels`/`powerUpLevels` rows survive.
- **Split writes.** Consumption, banking and the win bonus must land in one `saveHangarWarPayload` write. Mitigation: pure reducer plus a single persist, with a test that the balance and ownership cannot diverge.
- **Demo leakage.** An attract/demo run must never consume the player's war. Mitigation: the existing demo guard on `_saveHangarWarPayload`; test it.
- **Scope creep.** Auto-enable could grow into a full loadout-preset system; that is deliberately split into AH-0MWL8C6FE008G1E7. Price, win-bonus and ring-economy tuning stay out of scope.
- **Stale loadout references.** A save whose active loadout names items no longer owned is already filtered by `resolveActiveLoadout`; consumption must operate on resolved ids, not raw stored ids.

**Assumptions:** both outcomes consume the ship (Q2 = B); only deployed items are consumed (Q4 = B); the ring-end hangar-falls reset is unchanged; and "the ship" is the hangar's active loadout as shown, not the six-slot post-cap run set.

## Related work

- **AH-0MVUXCAW0001VUM6** — Capture cycle: hex deployment, boss-granted discovery and defending bot (the win path this item extends).
- **AH-0MVUXC2DD003HN0I** — Hangar War menu entry, mode separation and deployment (the deployment payload this item consumes).
- **AH-0MWEZZ9TE001577J** — Capture-cycle assault gate (the ring-end hangar-falls reset; deliberately unchanged).
- **AH-0MWH48IEG00929GQ** — Strengthen a hex's defence (a nearby economy change to co-ordinate with).
- **AH-0MVZJ6V1J001DA9D** — Hangar War deployments start with no extra weapons in the loadout (empty-loadout legality this item must preserve).
- **AH-0MWL8C6FE008G1E7** — Saved ship configurations: re-purchase and equip a known build in one action (the follow-on created from this intake; depends on this item).
- Docs: `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` (Candidate D persistence rules), `docs/Game Design Document.md` §8.2 (capture cycle), `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MWB8VFBC003743Y** – Requote docs and reconcile ring-timing guards (completed)
- **AH-0MWL8C6FE008G1E7** – Saved ship configurations: re-purchase and equip a known build in one action (blocked)
- **AH-0MWB8VDDI005WVMG** – Pin per-ring loadout resolution in tests (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: battle, build, cases, cores, defend (+28 more)
- `README.md` — matched: battle, build, cases, cores, defend (+27 more)
- `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` — matched: battle, build, cores, defend, earned (+25 more)

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — What should the hangar show after a hex battle (win or loss)?** — Answer (producer): **C, refined** — the deployed ship is genuinely consumed on both outcomes and **all its upgrades must be re-purchased**; when an upgrade is purchased it is **automatically enabled**. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q1 follow-on — add saved ship configurations?** — Answer (producer): **yes** — save ship configurations and select them from a drop-down to quickly purchase the needed upgrades. Created as **AH-0MWL8C6FE008G1E7**. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2 — Should winning and losing differ?** — Answer (producer): **B** — winning also consumes the deployed hull (it is left as the hex's defender); losing destroys it. The difference is economic: a win pays more salvage to equip a new ship. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3 — Bug or design change?** — Answer (producer): **B** — this is a design-change request, not a defect report. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q4 — After a hex battle, how much of the fleet must be re-purchased?** — Answer (producer): **B** — only the deployed ship is consumed: its equipped hull, equipped weapons, equipped modifiers and their levels are removed; owned items the player did not fly, and the free starter kit, survive. Source: interactive reply.

**Assumptions carried:** the free starter hull and starter weapon are always owned (no soft-lock); un-equip toggles remain available after an auto-equip; and the existing win bonus already supplies the "wins pay more" difference, so no new balance tuning is in scope.

## Traceability

- Duplicate check performed — no open or completed item covers ship consumption on battle completion; the closest items are the capture-cycle, assault-gate and defender items listed above, which this item extends rather than duplicates.

# Pre-emptive counter-push: defuse a pending frontier attack by deploying at its origin

Discovered from: the 2026-11-17 gameplay-mechanics review (rank 2 of 10; direction: create, **Low** priority — it depends on two sibling items).

## Goal (user story)

As a Hangar War player facing a queued attack on a hex I hold, I want to see that
attack before I deploy and to be able to strike its origin hex instead of waiting
to be hit, so that defending my ring is a decision I make rather than a report I
read afterwards.

## Problem statement

The between-sortie frontier tick resolves **at** the player. `runFrontierTick`
redistributes aggression, resolves queued `pendingAttacks`, and — when nothing is
queued and the seeded 70 % draw passes — attacks one held hex from its most
aggressive unheld neighbour. The player can only respond *after* the tick: there
is no way to see a pending attack before committing a deployment, and no way to
spend a deployment on pre-empting it. Defence is therefore read, not played.

Two sibling items already deliver the two halves this item sits on top of:

- **Strengthen a hexes defence (AH-0MWH48IEG00929GQ)** — spend banked salvage to
  upgrade a held hex's defending bot (the *reinforce* half).
- **Do not attack a hex from a hex the player is attacking (AH-0MWH3A87Z005LLOX)**
  — an attacked hex defends and cannot also strike (the *fairness* half).

What neither delivers is the **choice of tempo**: strike first, or hold and
absorb. That is this item.

Evidence of the gap:

- `HangarWarPayload.pendingAttacks` already exists and is persisted, but the map
  publishes it only after it has resolved (via the rolled-in defence report);
  `src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts` has no pre-deployment pending-attack surface.
- `runFrontierTick` resolves queued attacks with no awareness of which hex the
  player has chosen to attack, so a queued attack always lands (subject to the
  defender rating).
- `HangarWarDeployment.hexId` already names the deployment's target, so the
  decision input exists with no new payload field.

## The mechanic (full proposal)

1. **Publish the threat before the commitment.** On the hex map, a queued or
   imminent attack is drawn on the ring **before** the player deploys —
   origin hex, target hex, attacking force, the target defender's rating and the
   resulting margin — using the numbers the report already prints, only earlier.
   The `◀ HANGAR`/deploy flow stays one click.
2. **Deploying at the origin defuses it.** When a deployment whose `hexId` is the
   origin of a queued attack **wins** (its mini-boss is defeated), that queued
   attack is cancelled in the same capture payload write: the target hex is not
   attacked on this tick, and the report names the defusal ("_struck first at
   hex X — the attack on hex Y never launched_"). Losing the deployment changes
   nothing: the attack still resolves, so a failed pre-emption costs exactly a
   run.
3. **A visible trade.** The map states the trade at a glance: the origin's
   aggression, the defender it would leave un-upgraded, and the held hex that
   currently stands to be hit — so "strike first" versus "reinforce and hold" is
   an informed choice, the two being the same salvage in different places.
4. **No new battle model.** Everything stays arithmetic over stored numbers: a
   defusal removes a queued attack record; it never simulates hex-versus-hex
   combat, never adds a live defence, and never changes an existing force,
   aggression multiplier, jitter or margin.
5. **Pure and replayable.** The defusal rule lives in the shared frontier tick
   module as a parameter (`attackingHex`, already threaded by the sibling item),
   so a tick remains a pure function of `(payload, seed, tick, attackingHex)`
   and the same inputs replay identically. The map panel is rendered from the
   same pure intel module the report already uses.

## Why this improves player enjoyment

- It converts the outer loop's most passive moment ("here is what happened to
  you") into an active one ("here is what is about to happen — what will you
  do?").
- It gives a low-salvage player a real counter-play against the frontier
  treadmill that does not require out-buying the aggression budget.
- It makes the ring's two named failure modes — the treadmill and the opaque
  defence — answerable by the player's own sequencing, which is the difference
  between a war and a chore.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The hex map publishes a queued/imminent attack **before** deployment: origin,
   target, attacking force, defender rating and margin, read from the shipped
   pure intel module (no scene-local arithmetic, and no second copy of the
   resolver's formula).
2. A **winning** deployment whose target hex is the origin of a queued attack
   cancels that attack in the same payload write; the target hex's defence is
   not resolved on that tick and the rolled-in report announces the defusal.
3. A **losing** deployment at that origin leaves the queued attack intact and it
   resolves exactly as today.
4. An ordinary deployment (no queued attack at its origin) is byte-identical to
   today's tick: the existing `resolveDefence`, `attackingNeighbour` and
   `runFrontierTick` suites pass unchanged, and the 70 % attack-chance draw order
   is unchanged.
5. Both `PlayScene` tick paths carry the deployment's `hexId` (winning path at
   the mini-boss victory, losing path at the run-end handoff), as established by
   the sibling fairness item; the defusal is decided inside the pure tick, never
   in `PlayScene`.
6. No new persisted field: the decision input is the existing
   `HangarWarDeployment.hexId` and the existing `pendingAttacks`; a save written
   before this change loads and resolves exactly as today.
7. `GymHexWar` can queue an attack, declare the attacking hex and show both the
   pre-deployment threat panel and the defusal outcome through the shipped code
   path, with a row in `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`.
8. Automated tests pin: the pre-deployment panel content, defusal on a win,
   non-defusal on a loss, the no-change regression, both `PlayScene` paths, and
   replay determinism for `(payload, seed, tick, attackingHex)`.
9. Documentation: GDD §8.2 (the capture cycle and the defence report) and the
   new §8.3 entry, plus `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D's
   anti-checklist section.
10. The full project test suite passes (through the test skill).

## Impact

A player can see an incoming attack on the ring before spending a life and can
choose to strike the hex that is about to hit them instead, so holding the ring
becomes a sequence of decisions rather than a bill that arrives after each
sortie.

## Constraints and assumptions

- **Depends on the two siblings.** The reinforcement sink is delivered by
  AH-0MWH48IEG00929GQ and the fair-origin rule by AH-0MWH3A87Z005LLOX; this item
  adds only the pre-deployment threat surface and the defusal rule. It must be
  planned after both and must not re-implement either.
- **Arithmetic only.** No simulated battle, no new resolver, no new rating
  formula — the defence comparison is the shipped one.
- **One payload, no new fields.** No schema version bump; field-presence only.
- **Scope discipline.** Out of scope: rebalancing aggression, changing the 70 %
  attack chance, changing which held hex the frontier targets, and any live
  hex-versus-hex combat (there is none).
- **Determinism is a hard requirement** — a defusal may not consume or reorder
  seeded draws for an unchanged attacking hex.

## Key files (predicted)

- `src/core/hangarWar/hexDefence.ts` — the defusal rule inside `runFrontierTick`,
  parameterised by the attacking hex.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts` — the pre-deployment threat panel content.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts` / `src/scenes/HexMapScene.ts` — panel render
  and the deploy action.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — pass `hexId` on both tick paths, and announce the
  defusal on the landing map.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.ts` — the parity surface.
- GDD §8.2, §8.3; `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D.

## Related work

- Strengthen a hexes defence (AH-0MWH48IEG00929GQ) — dependency (the reinforce
  half of the same choice).
- Do not attack a hex from a hex the player is attacking (AH-0MWH3A87Z005LLOX) —
  dependency (threads the attacking hex and the fair-origin rule).
- Rebalance ring 1's grind budget: measured 16.4 min vs the authored 40–60 min
  window (AH-0MWFDQ9EY004NO4X) and Rebalance ring 2's grind budget: measured
  48.1 min vs the authored 90–120 min window (AH-0MWFDQCFV007BZE5) — a cheaper
  counter-play changes the measured line and both must be re-measured.
- The ring-end hangar assault and the frontier tick (GDD §8.2) — the
  arithmetic-only invariant this item preserves.

# Bot selection of upgrades are slower

## Problem statement

When the attract/demo bot is presented with the hold-full upgrade selection
overlay it picks an option after only **900 ms** (`BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS`),
so a viewer has no real chance to read the three offers before the bot has
already chosen — and once it chooses, the choice screen is torn down and only
the 3-2-1 countdown numeral remains, so nothing on screen says **which** item
the bot took. The bot's upgrade picks should dwell long enough to be watched
and should be visible on the countdown.

## Users

- **Attract/demo viewer** (the player watching the menu's 👁 Watch Demo
  attract run, or an idle-menu session): *"As a viewer of attract mode, I want
  to see the bot's upgrade options for a couple of seconds and then see which
  one it picked while the countdown plays, so the demo reads as a deliberate
  choice rather than an instant flicker."*
- **Player (human selection, incidental):** *"As a player, once I choose an
  upgrade I want to be reminded which one I took while the 3-2-1 countdown
  runs."* — the shared overlay tears its choice UI down on selection, so the
  chosen title is the only record during the countdown.
- **Designer / producer:** *"As a designer, I want the bot's overlay dwell to
  be one named, tunable constant so I can pace the demo without hunting magic
  numbers."*

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — **Bot dwell is 2.5 s.** In demo/attract mode the hold-full upgrade
  selection overlay (`MineralChoiceScene`) auto-selects only after a **2500 ms**
  pause, sourced from one named constant (`BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS` in
  `src/ai/botHumanLike.ts`, raised from 900); the bot therefore visibly shows
  the offered upgrades before choosing. Normal (non-demo) play still waits for a
  real pointer/keyboard selection and never auto-selects.
- AC2 — **Selected title under the countdown.** From the moment an option is
  selected until the countdown completes, the overlay renders the **chosen
  option's title** (its catalogue name, e.g. `Spread Shot Lv.3`) beneath the
  large 3-2-1 countdown numeral, and the title text is **destroyed** when the
  countdown finishes and the overlay closes — no title text, text object or
  tween outlives the overlay, and a fresh hold-full starts with no stale title.
- AC3 — **Countdown and resume are unchanged.** The selection still drives the
  existing beat-locked 3-2-1 countdown (2250 ms at the default 80 BPM) with its
  rising cue, the reduced-volume ghost fire still runs underneath, and the
  choice is still applied on the beat after "1" with the launcher's beat clock
  re-based. The title is purely additive presentation and never delays or
  alters selection, application or resume timing.
- AC4 — **Scope contained.** The mini-boss reward wheel's demo auto-spin delay
  is **not** changed by AC1 (it keeps its current separate delay/constant), and
  no other surface's timing changes; every gym that launches the shared overlay
  keeps its existing behaviour (no `autoSelectMs` passed) apart from gaining the
  title readout.
- AC5 — **Tests.** Unit tests in `src/scenes/__tests__/MineralChoiceScene.test.ts`
  cover: the chosen title is exposed and rendered while the countdown runs, and
  is gone (`null`) after the countdown completes; a manual selection shows its
  own title; the constant-pinned bot dwell is asserted (auto-select does not
  fire before 2500 ms and does fire after it). The demo integration test
  (`src/scenes/demoMode.integration.test.ts`) still asserts the
  selection → countdown → resume path and asserts the selected title is visible
  during the countdown. All existing overlay, gym-parity and countdown tests
  stay green.
- AC6 — **Docs.** `README.md` (attract/demo mode section) and
  `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§4.4 auto-select bullet and §4.5
  beat-locked-countdown bullet) are updated to state the **2.5 s** bot dwell
  and the selected title shown under the countdown (and removed with it).
- AC7 — **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
  including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site
  entries.**
- AC8 — **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Impact

A viewer of the attract-mode demo now gets a clear 2.5-second look at the bot's
three upgrade offers and can see exactly which one it took while the countdown
plays, instead of a near-instant pick that left no trace of the choice.

## Constraints

- Demo-only for the dwell: normal play must not gain any auto-selection
  (existing AC5 of AH-0MUXXQ1MN002RXGB must stay true).
- Tunables live in one shared place (`src/ai/botHumanLike.ts`), never as
  scattered magic numbers.
- The overlay keeps its single `onSelect` contract; it must not reach back into
  `PlayScene` by scene key.
- The countdown stays beat-derived (`createHoldFullCountdown` /
  `beatPeriodMs`), never a hard-coded 2250 ms.
- Headless test harnesses collapse text metrics to 0, so any title layout must
  keep a measurable fallback (mirroring the existing `CHOICE_*_LINE_HEIGHT`
  constants) and stay inside the 960 × 720 playfield.
- The overlay is shared by `PlayScene`, `HexMapScene`, `GymFormationScene`,
  `GymWeaponLeveling` and `GymPowerUpLeveling`; the title addition must keep
  gym↔game parity (no per-scene copies).

## Existing state

- `src/ai/botHumanLike.ts` exports `BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS = 900` — the
  demo dwell used for the hold-full choice auto-select, the mini-boss
  hold-full-style fallback choice, **and** the mini-boss wheel auto-spin
  (`PlayScene.openMiniBossReward` → `autoSpinMs`).
- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` (`init` → `autoSelectMs` /
  `autoSelectIndex`, `create` → `this.time.delayedCall`) auto-selects on the
  demo path. `select(index)` records the pending selection, tears down the
  whole choice UI (backdrop, heading, option labels/descriptions/details, the
  `★ New` badges, the `YOUR UPGRADES` panel, the keydown handler) and draws the
  large countdown numeral at `COUNTDOWN_Y = 270` (96 px, neon cyan).
  `completeSelection()` destroys the numeral, invokes `onSelect` and stops the
  scene. Public accessors already exist: `getCountdownText()`,
  `isCountdownActive()`, `isChoiceScreenVisible()`, `getOverlayElapsedMs()`.
- `src/scenes/core/holdFullCountdown.ts` owns the pure 3-2-1 scheduler
  (`HOLD_FULL_COUNTDOWN_COUNTS = 3`, `HOLD_FULL_COUNTDOWN_DURATION_MS`).
- `src/scenes/HexMapScene.ts` uses its own `demoDwellMs ?? HANGAR_WAR_TRAVERSAL_DWELL_MS`
  for demo reward overlays, so it does not depend on the bot choice constant.
- Docs pin the current 900 ms pace: `README.md` (attract/demo paragraph) and
  `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4 ("**900 ms**") and §4.5 (countdown tears
  the choice screen down, "leaving only the countdown numeral").
- Tests reference the constant symbolically (`BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS`), so
  a value change flows through `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` and
  `src/scenes/demoMode.integration.test.ts` waits without hard-coded numbers.

## Desired change

1. Raise the demo dwell to 2500 ms (`BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS`), keeping the
   mini-boss wheel's demo spin delay at its current pace via a separate constant
   so only the upgrade-selection pause slows.
2. In `MineralChoiceScene`, render the chosen option's title beneath the
   countdown numeral when a selection starts the countdown, expose it for tests
   (e.g. `getCountdownTitle()`), and destroy it alongside the numeral in
   `completeSelection()` (and defensively on shutdown).
3. Update the overlay's module doc comment, README and GDD to describe the
   2.5 s bot dwell and the title-under-countdown readout.
4. Cover the above with unit tests and keep the demo integration and gym-parity
   suites green.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ai/botHumanLike.ts` — raise `BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS` to 2500 and
  (if the wheel is scoped out) add a separate demo-spin delay constant; update
  the doc comment.
- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` — new countdown-title text object + layout
  constant, title creation in `select()`, destruction in `completeSelection()`
  and shutdown, `getCountdownTitle()` accessor, module doc comment.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — hold-full/mini-boss-fallback `autoSelectMs` wiring
  and the wheel `autoSpinMs` constant separation (comments mention the new
  pace).
- `src/scenes/__tests__/MineralChoiceScene.test.ts` — title-visible/title-cleared
  and 2500 ms dwell tests.
- `src/scenes/demoMode.integration.test.ts` — assert the selected title under
  the countdown on the demo path.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — only where the wheel/choice delay is asserted.
- `README.md` — attract/demo paragraph: 2.5 s dwell + selected title.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §4.4 auto-select bullet, §4.5 countdown
  bullet.

## Related work

- AH-0MUXXQ1MN002RXGB — *Demo bot: human-like input limits and complete the
  hold-full upgrade choice* (completed): introduced the demo auto-select and
  `BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS`.
- AH-0MV55OBKS006TL4N — *Demo/attract auto-select routes through the countdown*
  (completed): the bot's auto-select must drive the same selection → 3-2-1 →
  on-beat resume path.
- AH-0MV55OAQT004NMSN — *Beat-locked 3-2-1 countdown and on-beat resume*
  (completed): owns the countdown scheduler and the "numeral only" teardown this
  item extends with the chosen title.
- AH-0MVJ8U79V0056I2F — *AI bot does not know how to select upgrade in
  mini-boss reward screen* (completed): the mini-boss reward auto-select and
  wheel spin sharing the same demo delay.
- AH-0MUBVGI62004ED9Q — *Asteroids drop collectable minerals that fill the
  ship's hold and grant a power-up choice* (completed): the hold-full overlay
  itself.
- AH-0MV722WJS0075UTZ — countdown teardown of the choice UI (the behaviour the
  title readout complements).
- AH-0MV03GXZQ00801T4 / AH-0MW3MLV2V001NWBR — the retired Extra Life
  auto-select preference; the auto-select always takes option 0 today.

### Related work (automated report)

- **AH-0MVH80ZJ7009W18Z** – Some power-ups appear to do nothing (completed)
- **AH-0MV55OBKS006TL4N** – Demo/attract auto-select routes through the
  countdown (completed)
- **AH-0MVD20MYX0028JFL** – Close coverage gap: AC2 upgrade choices simulated
  (completed)

### Potentially related docs

- `README.md` (attract/demo mode paragraph) — documents the current 900 ms
  auto-select and the countdown/resume cadence.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4 (bot) and §4.5 (hold-full overlay) —
  the two canonical descriptions of this behaviour.
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — demo capture expectations that exercise the
  overlay.

## Assumptions and decisions for producer confirmation

- **A1 — Dwell scope.** The 2.5 s pause applies to the **upgrade selection
  overlay** only (hold-full choice, and the hold-full-style mini-boss
  fallback, which reuse `MineralChoiceScene`). The **mini-boss reward wheel**
  keeps its current demo auto-spin pace (split into its own constant), because
  the item describes an upgrade *selection* screen; the wheel has no selection
  and no titled options. *If the producer wants every bot reward overlay
  slowed to 2.5 s, AC4 is simply dropped and the wheel keeps the shared
  constant.*
- **A2 — Title scope.** The chosen title is shown for **every** selection on the
  shared overlay (bot auto-select and human), not bot-only: the choice UI is
  torn down for both, so the readout is equally useful and there is no penalty
  in normal play. *If bot-only is wanted, gate the title on the demo flag.*
- **A3 — Title copy.** The "title" is the option's catalogue `name` (e.g.
  `Spread Shot Lv.3`), i.e. the same text the option label carried (without the
  `1.` prefix), not the change summary or description.
- **A4 — Countdown timing unchanged.** The 3-2-1 countdown stays three beats
  (2250 ms at 80 BPM) and still applies the choice on the beat after "1".
- **A5 — Title lifetime.** The title clears when the countdown completes (the
  overlay closes); it is not carried into gameplay or the HUD.

## Risks

- **Scope creep** — "make the demo's pacing nicer" invites unrelated overlay
  restyling; anything beyond the dwell + title readout becomes a linked
  follow-up item, not this item.
- **Timing fragility** — lengthening the dwell changes total overlay duration
  (2500 + 2250 ms); integration tests that wait on constants remain valid, but
  any test with a hard-coded wait must move to `BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS`
  arithmetic.
- **Shared overlay regression** — the title must be torn down with the numeral
  in every exit path (completion, scene shutdown, scene restart) or a stale
  text object can leak between hold-fulls.
- **Wheel coupling** — `BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS` currently feeds the
  wheel's `autoSpinMs`; splitting it is the only way to keep AC4 true, so the
  split must be explicit and documented.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Should the 2.5 s pause apply to every bot reward overlay (hold-full
  choice, mini-boss wheel spin, hex-map demo reward overlays) or only the
  upgrade selection screen?"
  — Answer (agent, assumption A1, producer confirmation invited): only the
  upgrade selection overlay; the mini-boss wheel keeps its current delay via a
  separate constant. Source: work-item seed description ("the upgrade selection
  screen", "select whichever one they want") + repo inspection of
  `PlayScene.openMineralChoice` / `openMiniBossReward` / `HexMapScene`.
- Q: "Should the chosen title appear under the countdown for human selections
  too, or only for the bot?"
  — Answer (agent, assumption A2, producer confirmation invited): every
  selection on the shared overlay, because `select()` tears down the choice UI
  for both paths so the readout costs normal play nothing. Source: repo
  inspection of `MineralChoiceScene.select()` / `completeSelection()`.
- Q: "What is the 'title' — the option name, its change summary, or its
  description?"
  — Answer (agent, assumption A3): the catalogue option `name` (e.g.
  `Spread Shot Lv.3`), matching the label the option row showed. Source: seed
  wording "selected item's title" + `ChoiceOption` shape in
  `src/powerups/choice.ts`.
- Q: "Does the 3-2-1 countdown itself change length?"
  — Answer (agent, assumption A4): no — it stays beat-locked at three counts
  (2250 ms at the default 80 BPM) with the choice applied on the beat after
  "1". Source: `src/scenes/core/holdFullCountdown.ts` and
  AH-0MV55OAQT004NMSN.
- Q: "Which docs pin the current 900 ms pace?"
  — Answer (agent research): `README.md` attract/demo paragraph and
  `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4 ("**900 ms**") and §4.5 (countdown
  "leaving only the countdown numeral"). Both need updating.

# Record the gameplay-mechanics backlog in the GDD (§8.3) and the rejected-ideas appendix (§11)

Discovered from: the 2026-11-17 gameplay-mechanics review. The four new
mechanics from that review were filed as their own items; this item tracks the
**GDD documentation** of the whole review so a later commit has a work-item
association.

## Goal (user story)

As a designer or agent reading the GDD, I want the review's accepted mechanics
and its rejected ones recorded in one place, each pointing at the authoritative
work item, so that a proposal is never mistaken for shipped behaviour and a
rejected idea is never silently re-proposed.

## What was written (already applied to the working tree)

`docs/Game Design Document.md`:

1. **New §8.3 — *Proposed gameplay mechanics (backlog — recorded 2026-11-17)*.**
   Records the six accepted mechanics in rank order with, for each: the loop
   tier, the gap it closes (with the section or code evidence), the mechanic
   rule and its tunables, the legibility requirement, why it pleases, and the
   measurement that gates it. Entries: Graze and Danger Multiplier (rank 10,
   High, AH-0MWL7ORK8007LXJI); Weapon evolutions (rank 8, Medium,
   AH-0MWL7OWPF003E4TP); Anomaly (elite) enemies and wave twists (rank 7,
   Medium, AH-0MWL7P1AO003LKXT); Beat-locked soundtrack and intensity mix
   (rank 6, already planned, AH-0MVKXT7O70061FXU / AH-0MVMH2OPY001X6M3);
   Matchup combat from hex intel (rank 5, already planned,
   AH-0MWL5376H001WJFZ); Pre-emptive counter-push (rank 2, Low,
   AH-0MWL7P5T50030229).
2. **New §11 — *Appendix: Gameplay mechanics considered but not implemented*.**
   Records the four **rejected** proposals — Manual Overdrive (rank 9), Focus
   mode and visible hit core (rank 4), Extraction banking (rank 3), Run grade
   and medals (rank 1) — each with what it was, why it was rejected, and what
   evidence or prerequisite would revive it, plus a disposition table covering
   all ten proposals.
3. **Four short normative pointers**, each a blockquote saying "Proposed, not
   shipped" and naming the §8.3 entry and work item, so a reader of the
   specification finds the backlog where it would land: §4.4 (weapon
   evolutions), §4.5 (graze scoring), §4.6 (anomaly elites as a third
   difficulty axis) and §8.2 *The defence resolver and the frontier tick*
   (pre-emptive counter-push).

## Acceptance criteria

1. §8.3 exists with a subsection per accepted mechanic, each naming its work
   item id (with title) and its priority, and the section states plainly that
   nothing in it is shipped or scheduled.
2. §11 exists as the appendix of rejected ideas, with a per-idea rejection
   rationale and revival condition, and a disposition table covering all ten
   proposals exactly once, with the accepted rows matching the work items.
3. The four normative pointers exist and are consistent with §8.3 (same work
   item ids, same claims), and no normative table was changed as if the
   proposals were shipped.
4. Section numbering is intact: §9 (clarifying Q&A) and §10 (validation
   checklist) are unchanged, and §11 follows §10 with the end-of-document line
   last.
5. Existing documentation guard tests still pass unchanged — in particular
   `src/powerUpWeaponRosterDocs.test.ts` (its §8 slice only requires containment
   of the classic-arcade roster and deferrals) and
   `src/ai/eval/experienceValidationDocs.test.ts` (GDD §2.7 text untouched).
6. The full project test suite passes (run through the test skill, never an ad
   hoc invocation).

## Status note

The documentation change is **already committed on `dev` as `df5d3d3c`**
("add additional gameplay mechanic ideas", +277 lines, `docs/Game Design
Document.md` only, zero lines removed) and is **unpushed** — `origin/dev..dev`
holds it plus the unrelated `ff09d1b0`. It was made in the main checkout during
the review session rather than in an `implement.py` worktree, and the commit
carries **no work-item association**.

Landing it therefore needs an `implement.py` worktree session that verifies the
content is already correct (nothing to re-apply), records the work-item
association (commit or comment naming this id — see the review comment below for
the exact commit), and lets the gated push carry the commit to `origin/dev`.

**Key Files:**

- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — the only file changed (§8.3, §11 and the four
  "Proposed, not shipped" pointers).
- `src/powerUpWeaponRosterDocs.test.ts` — existing guard test; its §8 slice is
  containment-only, so the new §8.3 must not remove the recorded roster or the
  deferred candidates.
- `src/ai/eval/experienceValidationDocs.test.ts` — existing guard test; requires
  the GDD §2.7 heading and text to stay untouched.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-18 — `plan` (auto-complete path, effort Extra Small / risk Low): ran
  the six review stages against the existing content. Corrected the stale
  "Status note" (the change is committed as `df5d3d3c`, not uncommitted),
  added the `**Key Files:**` section and this changelog. No acceptance criterion
  changed.

## Impact

A reader of the GDD now sees, in one section, which gameplay mechanics are
proposed and who owns each one, and sees in the appendix which ideas were turned
down and why — so the design record cannot be mistaken for shipped behaviour and
rejected proposals stay rejected with their reasoning intact.

## Constraints

- Documentation only: no source, config or data change.
- The proposal text in each work item is authoritative; §8.3 summarises and
  links, and must not drift into a second specification.
- UK English, matching the surrounding document.

- **AH-0MVNSSY9L001P1CC** – We need an outer loop (completed)

- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: acceptance, agent, already, applied, arcade (+157 more)

**Phase 1 of 5 — implementation.** Parent: AH-0MWL5376H001WJFZ (AC1, AC2, AC3, AC14).

## Goal

As the implementer, I want one pure, headless matchup rule that decides
`effective` / `neutral` / `resisted` from an injectable verdict lookup, and
load-time validation that makes a bad authored list fail loudly, so the rule has
exactly one home and the authored data is trustworthy.

## Context

Parent decision Q1 = A + B: **A is the rule**. Q3 = ×2 / ×0.5. Q4 = (a) the
authored lists stay authoritative, but the resolver takes a verdict lookup so a
type-derived default can land later behind the same seam. Q5 = normalise
`waveLaser` → `wave_laser` through one shared mapping and validate loudly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `src/core/hangarWar/hexMatchup.ts` exports a pure, headless `resolveHexMatchup` returning `'effective' | 'neutral' | 'resisted'`; total for `null`/`undefined`/unknown ids (neutral) and for an unauthored hex (neutral).
- The lookup is an injectable "verdict for a weapon id" shape, with a helper that builds it from the normalised authored lists; a synthetic lookup fully replaces it with no edit to any consumer.
- A pure, deterministic ledger accrues resisted credit — one hit point per two connected shots, credit to the second of each pair — bounded per target and per weapon, with no new RNG consumption.
- `validateRingDefinitions` (or its successor) normalises every authored entry through the shared grant-style mapping and throws at load on an unknown catalogue id or a same-hex overlap, naming the hex id and the offending entry.
- No scene or entity imports `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts` to decide a verdict; the authored data reaches combat only through the lookup hand-off.
- `npm run build` passes and the Phase 1 tests are green.


### Parent acceptance-criteria trace

- (AC1) The implementation matches the producer's decisions — Q1's A-rule/B-presentation split is visible in where the rule lives (pure resolver at the hit seam) and where the deflect presentation lives (impact-feedback seam). All decisions Q1–Q5 recorded on the parent are honoured.
- (AC2) A **pure, headless** matchup resolver lives in `src/core/hangarWar/` and is the only place the advantage/handicap is decided; unit-tested for `effective` / `neutral` / `resisted`, for an **unknown weapon id** (neutral, total) and for an **unauthored hex** (neutral). Its input is a **verdict lookup for a weapon id**, not a direct scan of the authored lists, so a type-derived default can be introduced later without touching the combat seam.
- (AC3) The authored `strengths`/`weaknesses` are **normalised to catalogue weapon ids** and validated: an id that resolves to no catalogue weapon, or a weapon that appears in **both** lists of the same hex, fails loudly at load (`validateRingDefinitions` or its successor), with a test per failure mode.
- (AC14) **Nothing survives that would block approach C later:** the resolver's verdict lookup is injectable and tested with a synthetic lookup (no authored data), proving the rule is decoupled from the lists' storage — a follow-up can swap the lookup's backing table for a damage-type table without editing `CombatScene` or the impact seam.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add `hexMatchup.ts` with the verdict type, the lookup shape, `resolveHexMatchup` and the ledger.
- Reuse the existing `waveLaser` → `wave_laser` alias convention (`GRANT_ALIASES` in `captureCycle.ts`) rather than inventing a second mapping table.
- Extend the `strengths`/`weaknesses` branch of `validateRingDefinitions` with id-resolution and overlap checks.
- Keep the module free of Phaser, scene and DOM imports.

## Deliverables

- New pure module `src/core/hangarWar/hexMatchup.ts`
- Validation extended in `src/core/hangarWar/hexRing.ts`
- Phase 1 tests green

**Key Files:**

- `src/core/hangarWar/hexMatchup.ts`
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexRing.ts`
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexRing.test.ts`
- `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts`
- `src/utils/weapons.ts`
- `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts`
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexMatchup.test.ts`

## Dependencies

Depends on Phase 1 tests (red-first).

## Assumption to document

The shared `waveLaser` → `wave_laser` alias is the normalisation of record. Any
authored entry the alias table does not cover and the catalogue does not hold
must fail load, not pass through silently.

**Phase 2 of 5 — test-first.** Parent: AH-0MWL5376H001WJFZ (AC5, AC6, AC14).

## Goal

Write the **failing** tests that pin "every player damage source honours one
rule" and the measured ×2 / ×0.5 effect, before the charge is wired anywhere.

## Context — a correction to the parent's stated seam

The parent description asserts `CombatScene.damageEnemyWithBullet` is "the
single seam every player damage source funnels through". **That is not true for
the mini-boss**, which is this item's primary scope target (Q2 = mini-boss +
`health` > 1 elites). Verified in the current tree:

- `CombatScene.damageEnemyWithBullet` — ordinary bullets and damage-budget beams (wave laser)
- `CombatScene.damageEnemyViaAoe` — AOE detonations against enemies
- `PlayScene.onPlayerBulletHitsBoss` → `_damageBoss` — the Boss via a bullet
- `PlayScene.onPlayerBulletHitsBoss` → `_damageMiniBoss` — the **MiniBoss** via a bullet
- `PlayScene.onAoeHitsBoss` → `_damageBoss` — the Boss via AOE

There are therefore **five** entry points across two classes, and the
`onAoeHitsBoss(x, y, radius)` signature carries **no weapon identity at all**.
The tests in this item must cover each path explicitly, so the implementation
cannot satisfy AC5 by wiring only the bullet-vs-enemy seam.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A test proves the verdict reaches the same damage outcome for each path: ordinary bullet, damage-budget beam (wave laser), AOE detonation, mini-boss bullet, mini-boss AOE.
- A measurement test pins the magnitudes: against the same mini-boss phase, the effective weapon kills **at least 1.8× faster** and the resisted weapon **at least 1.8× slower** than the neutral weapon — asserted numerically, not in prose.
- A test proves chaff (`health` = 1) takes exactly today's damage under every verdict (Q2 scope guard).
- A test proves the resisted ledger is per-target and per-weapon and never charges more than one hit point per two connected shots, including a target killed mid-pair.
- A determinism test proves a replay of the same shot sequence against the same seed lands an identical hit count (no new RNG-stream consumption).
- Every new test is **red** against the current tree.


### Parent acceptance-criteria trace

- (AC5) Every player damage source honours the multiplier: ordinary bullets, damage-budget beams (wave laser), AOE detonations and the per-matchup ledger share the one rule; a test proves each source is affected identically.
- (AC6) **Measured effect:** against the same mini-boss phase, the effective weapon kills **at least 1.8× faster** and the resisted weapon **at least 1.8× slower** than the neutral weapon, asserted in a headless test with the chosen magnitudes (so the numbers are pinned, not prose).

## Minimal Implementation

- Create test file(s) only — no production wiring in this item.
- Drive the five paths through their real seams (scene-level tests where the boss/mini-boss path demands it), not through re-implemented arithmetic.
- Express the 1.8× measurement as a ratio against a neutral baseline measured in the same test run.

## Deliverables

- Hit-charge and damage-source test file(s) (red)
- Mini-boss / boss AOE path covered explicitly

**Key Files:**

- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.test.ts`
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.hexMiniBossProfile.test.ts`
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.hexMiniBossVictory.test.ts`
- `src/entities/PlayerBullet.ts`
- `src/entities/MiniBoss.ts`
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts`
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexMatchup.ts`

## Dependencies

Depends on the pure resolver landing (Phase 1 implementation).

**Phase 2 of 5 — implementation.** Parent: AH-0MWL5376H001WJFZ (AC1, AC4, AC5, AC6).

## Goal

As the player, I want the weapon I brought to actually matter — the counter
weapon tears through a mini-boss and the weapon it resists barely scratches it —
so my pre-deployment reading pays off.

## Context

This is the **A rule** landing in combat. The verdict must reach the run through
the existing hex→run hand-off (`HexBossProfile` →
`hexMiniBossConfigForLevel`) and be applied by **one** shared charge helper, so
no scene re-derives it.

Per the Phase 2 test item, there are **five** damage entry points, and the
mini-boss is on `PlayScene._damageMiniBoss` — not on
`CombatScene.damageEnemyWithBullet` as the parent description assumed. The
`onAoeHitsBoss(x, y, radius)` signature must grow an optional weapon id so the
AOE-vs-boss path can honour the rule at all.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `PlayerBullet` carries the shot's weapon id, set on every spawn path (ordinary bullet, split warhead, damage-budget beam), so identity is available at the hit.
- One shared charge helper is the **only** place a verdict becomes hit points; `damageEnemyWithBullet`, `damageEnemyViaAoe`, `_damageBoss` and `_damageMiniBoss` (and the `onPlayerBulletHitsBoss` / `onAoeHitsBoss` entry points) all route through it.
- The resolved matchup reaches the run via `HexBossProfile` → `hexMiniBossConfigForLevel`, so the game, the attract run and every gym read one value.
- Chaff (`health` = 1) takes exactly today's damage under every verdict.
- No new randomness and no new RNG-stream consumption: a replay of the same payload/seed lands the same hits.
- `npm run build` passes and the Phase 2 tests are green.


### Parent acceptance-criteria trace

- (AC4) The resolved matchup reaches the run **through the existing hex→run hand-off** (`HexBossProfile` → `hexMiniBossConfigForLevel`), so the game, the attract run and every gym read one value — no scene re-derives it.
- (AC5) Every player damage source honours the multiplier: ordinary bullets, damage-budget beams (wave laser), AOE detonations and the per-matchup ledger share the one rule; a test proves each source is affected identically.
- (AC6) **Measured effect:** against the same mini-boss phase, the effective weapon kills **at least 1.8× faster** and the resisted weapon **at least 1.8× slower** than the neutral weapon, asserted in a headless test with the chosen magnitudes (so the numbers are pinned, not prose).

## Minimal Implementation

- Add `weaponId` to `PlayerBullet` beside `impactFx`; populate it where `impactFx` is already assigned in the shared spawn paths.
- Publish the hex's verdict lookup on `HexBossProfile` and carry it into `hexMiniBossConfigForLevel`.
- Add one protected charge helper on `CombatScene` (ledger-backed, calling the pure resolver) and make the four damage methods call it; extend `onAoeHitsBoss` with the weapon id.
- Reset the ledger entry for a target when it dies; key the ledger by target + weapon only.

## Deliverables

- Weapon identity plumbed onto the shot
- One shared charge helper across all five entry points
- Matchup published on `HexBossProfile` and carried into the mini-boss config

**Key Files:**

- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`
- `src/entities/PlayerBullet.ts`
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexBoss.ts`
- `src/waves/miniBossDesigns.ts`
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexMatchup.ts`

## Dependencies

Depends on the Phase 2 tests (red-first) and the pure resolver.

## Assumptions to document

- The five separate entry points are consolidated behind one helper rather than merged into a single method; merging them would be a far larger refactor and is out of scope.
- Extending `onAoeHitsBoss` with an optional weapon id is additive: an omitted id resolves neutral, so existing callers keep today's behaviour.

**Phase 3 of 5 — test-first.** Parent: AH-0MWL5376H001WJFZ (AC7, AC8, AC9).

## Goal

Write the **failing** tests that pin what the three states look and sound like,
so the presentation cannot ship as untested juice.

## Context

This is the **B presentation** half of Q1 = A + B: the resisted state must read
as *wrong tool*, never as *broken gun*. Every assertion is on a published
mapping or a published reaction flag — never a pixel diff.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A state→cue test asserts effective and resisted each map to a **different** cue at a **different playback rate** than neutral, and that every mapped cue exists in `PLAYER_WEAPON_IMPACT_CUES` and in `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`.
- A state→spec test asserts effective and resisted map to **different** `ImpactFxSpec`s that differ in **shape as well as colour**, and that the neutral spec is byte-identical to today's per-weapon `impactFx`.
- A test asserts the flinch asymmetry through a published/animated reaction flag: the boss reacts to an effective hit and shows **no** reaction to a resisted hit.
- A test asserts no state is silent and that the three states remain distinguishable with colour removed (distinct shape + distinct pitch).
- A test asserts the "RESISTED" tag fires **once per encounter** (the first resisted hit only), never per hit, with a bar pip thereafter.
- Every new test is **red** against the current tree.


### Parent acceptance-criteria trace

- (AC7) **Felt effect (SFX):** effective and resisted states play **different cues at different playback rates** than neutral, the cues exist in the ToneForge cue map, and a test asserts the state→cue mapping; no state is silent.
- (AC8) **Felt effect (VFX):** effective and resisted states spawn **different impact specs** (colour *and* shape, not colour alone), and a test asserts the state→spec mapping plus that neutral is byte-identical to today's per-weapon `impactFx`.
- (AC9) **Non-flinch/flinch asymmetry:** the boss shows a visible reaction to an effective hit and **none** to a resisted hit (testable through a published/animated reaction flag rather than pixel diffing).

## Minimal Implementation

- Create test file(s) only — no presentation code in this item.
- Assert against the shared impact seam (`resolveImpactFx` / `resolveWeaponImpactFx`) and the cue dispatcher (`playWeaponImpactCue`).
- Express the shape assertion on a published shape/primitive discriminator, not on graphics commands.

**Phase 3 of 5 — implementation.** Parent: AH-0MWL5376H001WJFZ (AC7, AC8, AC9).

## Goal

As the player, I want to *hear* and *see* whether my weapon is the right tool
within seconds of the first hit — a brighter, sharper, higher-pitched impact
that makes the boss flinch for the counter weapon, and a dull clang that barely
moves it for the weapon it resists.

## Context

The B presentation of Q1 = A + B. Audio must be baked through the existing
ToneForge pipeline and routed through the one shared impact dispatcher — never
synthesised ad hoc in a scene. Neutral must stay byte-for-byte today's
behaviour.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Effective and resisted each spawn their own impact spec through the shared impact seam, differing in **colour and shape** (e.g. bright shard burst vs. dull ring / spall), not colour alone.
- New cue(s) are baked via the ToneForge pipeline, mapped in `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`, and dispatched through `playWeaponImpactCue`; existing per-weapon cues are pitch-shifted at the call site rather than re-baked.
- The boss/mini-boss shows a bounded positional kick plus a white silhouette flash on an effective hit, and **no** flinch on a resisted hit.
- A one-shot "RESISTED" tag appears on the first resisted hit of an encounter, with a small bar pip thereafter.
- Neutral is unchanged for every weapon.
- `npm run build` passes and the Phase 3 tests are green.


### Parent acceptance-criteria trace

- (AC7) **Felt effect (SFX):** effective and resisted states play **different cues at different playback rates** than neutral, the cues exist in the ToneForge cue map, and a test asserts the state→cue mapping; no state is silent.
- (AC8) **Felt effect (VFX):** effective and resisted states spawn **different impact specs** (colour *and* shape, not colour alone), and a test asserts the state→spec mapping plus that neutral is byte-identical to today's per-weapon `impactFx`.
- (AC9) **Non-flinch/flinch asymmetry:** the boss shows a visible reaction to an effective hit and **none** to a resisted hit (testable through a published/animated reaction flag rather than pixel diffing).

## Minimal Implementation

- Add the two new impact specs beside the existing per-weapon `ImpactFxSpec` definitions.
- Bake the new cue family and register it in `PLAYER_WEAPON_IMPACT_CUES` and the cue-mapping doc.
- Add the flinch reaction to the shared boss/mini-boss hit path, gated on the verdict, with a bounded magnitude so dense fire never stutters.
- Keep the one-shot tag state on the encounter, not on the scene's per-frame path.

## Deliverables

- Two new impact specs (effective / resisted) with distinct shape and colour
- New baked cue family plus cue-mapping doc entry
- Bounded flinch reaction, one-shot RESISTED tag

**Key Files:**

- `src/utils/weapons.ts`
- `src/audio/effects.ts`
- `src/vfx/bulletImpact.ts`
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`
- `src/entities/Boss.ts`
- `src/entities/MiniBoss.ts`
- `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`

## Dependencies

Depends on the Phase 3 tests (red-first) and the matchup charge landing.

## Assumption to document

The flinch is a bounded positional kick plus a silhouette flash, not a new
animation state machine; approach E (the weakness stagger meter) is a linked
follow-up, not scope here.
