# Seeded procedural ring content generator

## Goal

Add the runtime **content** generator that replaces the authored ring table:
for any ring index, derive a complete, valid `HexRingDefinition`-shaped ring
from the war's seeded RNG.

**User story:** As a player, every war's hex map is generated from its seed, so
the frontier never stops at the last authored ring and the same seed replays
the same map.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Generated ring content is a **pure, deterministic function of `(payload.seed, ringIndex)`**: the same seed/ring yields identical hexes (ids, coordinates, boss, strengths/weaknesses, grant, base aggression and variety axes), and at least two distinct seeds yield materially different rings.
- Every generated ring satisfies the shipped design invariants, validated loudly rather than repaired: exactly one weapon hex and it is the ring's hardest, one special-mission hex granting a hull, at least one beatable hex, unique ids and coordinates, and the aggression band/budget rules.
- `src/core/hangarWar/rng.ts` exposes a per-ring and per-hex derived stream (mirroring `specialRotationSeed`), so a change in one ring or one hex cannot shift another ring's map; no second RNG generator is introduced (draws come from `createHangarWarRng` / `createSeededRng` over `normaliseSeed`).
- The generator is a pure core function in `src/core/hangarWar/hexRing.ts` (or a sibling module it exports through) with no Phaser, storage or scene import; `validateRingDefinitions` / `generateRing` stay the validation and ordering seams the generator feeds, and an invalid generated ring throws `HexRingDefinitionError` rather than being repaired.
- Personalities, contracts and landmarks are drawn from the existing bounded vocabularies (`HEX_PERSONALITY_IDS`, `HEX_LANDMARK_IDS`) and shared mechanics only: at most one weapon hex and one special-mission hex per ring, no new combat implementation, and hex ids stay unique within the ring and stable across reloads (`hex-r<ring>-<n>` identity is derived from the same seed and ring index).
- Boss identities are generated from a deterministic, seed-derived identity pool that keeps telemetry traceable (stable for a seed, distinct enough across hexes), and every hex's strengths/weaknesses name real shipped weapon/vocabulary ids.
- The contract tests added by `Tests: ring generation determinism and invariant contract` pass with their `it.fails` markers flipped to plain `it` (no leftover `it.fails` remains).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Notes & assumptions

- **Validation cadence (documented assumption):** the generator validates the
  ring it produced once per generation (a ring open, or a definitions lookup),
  via `validateRingDefinitions`, and throws on any issue. Broad many-seed
  coverage lives in the contract tests rather than in every materialisation.
- **Tutorial variance:** per producer Q1 = B, ring 1 generates from the seed
  like every other ring, so the opening ring varies per war. A fixed tutorial
  ring would be a separate producer decision.
- Draw order is the determinism contract: any later change to field order or
  draw count is a deliberate golden-fixture update, never a silent re-roll.

**Key Files:**

- `src/core/hangarWar/hexRing.ts` — the seeded ring-content generator; keep `validateRingDefinitions` / `generateRing` / `ringCoordinates` / `ringSize` pure and reuse them.
- `src/core/hangarWar/rng.ts` — the per-ring/per-hex derived streams (`ringContentSeed`, per-hex mixing).
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexBoss.ts` — boss profile seam the generated identity must resolve through.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexDifficulty.ts` — `MAX_HEX_AGGRESSION`, `beatableAggressionCeiling`, `hexAggressionLevel`: the aggression band the generator must honour.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexDefence.ts` — `authoredRingBaseMass` / `ringAggressionBudget` / `redistributeAggression`: the budget rules generated rings must satisfy.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexRingGeneration.contract.test.ts` — flip the `it.fails` markers and keep the contract green.
- `src/core/hangarWar/__fixtures__/ringGenerationGolden.ts` — the pinned golden sequence.

## Related work

- Parent **AH-0MWL4SNKR001CDAA** — Procedurally generated Hex Map (epic).
- **AH-0MWJ4ZDXO007VDJS** — hand-authored ring-1 landmark/contract the generator
  must now derive instead of author.
- **AH-0MWEW5I1F006CLCH** — ring landmarks (`fortress`, `cache`) the generator
  may assign at most one of each.

# Grant economy with level-scaling repeats

## Goal

Make every grant a generated ring hands out a **real effect**, even when a
large ring needs more grants than the hangar catalogue holds.

**User story:** As a player, every hex promises something real: a new hull or
weapon early, and a genuine weapon/power-up level (or a mineral payout) once I
already own everything — never a silent no-op reward.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Grant economy:** the generator prefers unowned catalogue entries; when a ring exhausts them it cycles level-capable entries and each repeat raises the weapon/power-up level (capped at `MAX_LEVEL`), while unlevellable repeats (hull/modifier) bank a mineral payout; every granted hex resolves to a real effect (never a silent no-op).
- Grant selection is deterministic for `(seed, ringIndex, hex)` and reads the fleet's current owned sets (`weaponLevels` / `powerUpLevels` / unlocked hulls and modifiers) as an input, so the preference order is reproducible and does not consume an extra draw when nothing is owned.
- `withGrantedEntry` (or the capture seam that calls it) applies the level-scaling repeat rule: a repeat of a level-capable entry writes an effective level row above the base (the shipped `weaponLevels` / `powerUpLevels` "first purchase records 2" convention) capped at `MAX_LEVEL`, instead of only adding an already-owned id.
- An unlevellable repeat (hull or modifier with no level dimension) banks its payout through the shipped banking rule (`bankSalvage` / `salvageBanking.ts`) rather than granting nothing, and a replay of an already-held hex cannot double-count it (the stored held/granted marker guards it).
- A property test over many seeds and ring indices asserts that `resolveHexGrant` returns a non-null result for every generated hex's `grants` id and that the reported `kind` matches the catalogue entry — no generated grant is an unknown id or a silent no-op.
- Unit tests cover: preference for unowned entries; exhaustion then cycling; level raise on a level-capable repeat; cap at `MAX_LEVEL`; mineral payout on an unlevellable repeat; determinism of the chosen grant for a seed.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Notes & assumptions

- **Assumption (documented in the intake and non-blocking):** a repeat of an
  entry with no level dimension (hull/modifier) banks the shipped mineral
  payout instead of levelling. The epic's own acceptance criterion states this,
  so it is implemented as written; a producer correction is a follow-up, not a
  blocker.
- `MAX_LEVEL` is the campaign level cap (10); the repeat rule caps at the same
  value so a deep ring cannot create an uncapped upgrade.
- Scope guard: no new catalogue vocabulary or effect kinds — only assignment
  and level scaling of the shipped entries.

**Key Files:**

- `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts` — `resolveHexGrant`, `withGrantedEntry`, the capture path that banks contract/cache payouts (the banking precedent to reuse).
- `src/core/hangarWar/salvageBanking.ts` — the shipped banking rule for the unlevellable-repeat payout.
- `src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts` — the grant pool (`hull` / `weapon` / `modifier` entries) the generator draws from.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexRing.ts` — the generator's grant assignment (consumes the pool and the owned sets).
- `src/core/GameState.ts` — `MAX_LEVEL` and the level conventions the repeat rule must respect.
- `src/core/hangarWar/types.ts` — `weaponLevels` / `powerUpLevels` row shapes written by a repeat.
- `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.test.ts` — grant application tests.

## Related work

  producer decision (cycle real catalogue grants with level scaling).

# Seed-aware ring definitions source and id lookup

## Goal

Give every runtime consumer one seed-aware seam for "the definitions of this
ring" and "the definition of this hex id", so no consumer needs the authored
table and a looked-up hex always matches the ring the war is playing.

**User story:** As a test/agent, definition lookup by hex id is derivable from
the same seed as the ring, so intel, the special-mission rotation, the defence
resolver and the harness can never disagree about what a hex is.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A single pure source seam exists (e.g. `ringDefinitionsFor(seed, ringIndex)` and `findRingDefinition(seed, ringIndex, hexId)` exported alongside the generator) that returns the generated definitions for the war's `payload.seed`; every default currently reading `HEX_RING_DEFINITIONS` / `hexRingDefinitionsFor` / `findHexRingDefinition` is wired to it.
- Definition lookup by hex id is derived from the generated ring, not from a static table: `buildHexMapModel`, `specialMissionRingView` / `specialMissionOfferFor`, `authoredRingBaseMass` (and the `attackerType` boss lookup) and `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts` all consult the seam and receive the same definitions the ring state was materialised from.
- An injected `definitions` option still wins over the default (tests and gym overrides keep working), and passing definitions for a different ring cannot leak into a lookup (the source is keyed by ring index).
- Any remaining import of authored ring content from a non-test, non-fixture module is removed; `grep` for `HEX_RING_DEFINITIONS` outside the retirement item's own cleanup finds no runtime consumer.
- Unit tests assert that intel, the special-mission rotation and the aggression base mass agree with the generated ring for several seeds and rings, including a ring index above 2.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Notes & assumptions

- The seam takes the **seed** (a number), never the whole payload, so the core
  stays pure and a caller can resolve a future ring's intel without mutating
  state.
- A ring index above the old authored ceiling must already work here (the
  generator is the whole content source); the frontier/migration behaviour is
  the next item's concern.
- Do not delete `HEX_RING_DEFINITIONS` in this item — the retirement item owns
  that removal plus the fixture/scene/test migration, so this item can land
  green with the authored table still present but unused by the seams it owns.

**Key Files:**

- `src/core/hangarWar/hexRing.ts` — the generator and the new definitions-source exports.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts` — `buildHexMapModel` / `pickAttractHex` defaults and the by-id definition fallback.
- `src/core/hangarWar/specialMission.ts` — `specialMissionRingView` / `specialMissionOfferFor` defaults.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexDefence.ts` — `authoredRingBaseMass` and the defender `attackerType` boss lookup.
- `src/core/hangarWar/types.ts` — `HangarWarPayload.seed` (the generation seed source).
- `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts` — the harness definitions lookup.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.test.ts`, `src/core/hangarWar/specialMission.test.ts` — consumer agreement tests.

  this seam replaces.

# On-demand materialisation and an unlimited frontier

## Goal

Remove the authored-successor ceiling from ring progression: opening the next
ring generates it from the seed for **any** ring index, so a war never stalls.

**User story:** As a player, securing a ring always opens the next, bigger ring
— ring 3, ring 4 and beyond — because the successor is generated on demand
rather than waiting for authored data.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `materialiseRing` generates the ring from `payload.seed` when the stored ring is empty (a fresh war) and returns a stored ring unchanged when it holds any hexes — never re-rolling, padding or discarding.
- `openNextRing` succeeds for every ring index from 1 upward (asserted through at least ring 10): it generates the successor ring from the seed, appends it to the carried hexes exactly as today, reports `opened: true` and the new `ringIndex`, and no longer leaves the ring secured because an authored successor is missing.
- Ring advancement is exercised end-to-end (secure or rush a ring → next ring opens → its hexes are displayable, capturable and taggable by intel) in an integration test that reaches at least ring 4.
- The aggression budget for a generated ring is derived from that ring's generated base mass (`authoredRingBaseMass` reads the same source as materialisation), so the frontier tick's mass, floor and beatable-hex guarantee hold for rings above 2.
- The `try`/`catch` around a missing authored ring in `createRingState` is replaced by generation for a positive ring index; a non-positive or corrupt ring index still degrades safely rather than throwing mid-render.
- Existing ring-advance behaviour is preserved: a rush past unheld hexes keeps those hexes (held state, defender, aggression) in the payload, and the ring-end hangar assault gate still runs before any advance.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Notes & assumptions

- The stored-ring invariant is absolute: a non-empty `ring.hexes` array is never
  regenerated, so a save's seen map can never change under the player (see the
  save-compatibility item for the defensive-parse half).
- Rush/secure semantics are unchanged: only *where the successor content comes
  from* changes, not when a ring opens.
- This item may keep the authored table present (retirement is the following
  item) but must not require it to exist for progression.

**Key Files:**

- `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts` — `materialiseRing`, `openNextRing`, `createRingState` call sites and the ring-advance result.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexRing.ts` — `createRingState` gains the seed-aware generation path.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexDefence.ts` — `authoredRingBaseMass` / `ringAggressionBudget` feeding off the generated base mass.
- `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.test.ts` — ring-advance and materialisation tests.
- `src/core/hangarWar/__fixtures__/aggressionScenarios.ts` — the harness's synthesised "ring 3+" shape can now use the real generator.
- `src/scenes/hangarWarTraversal.integration.test.ts` — multi-ring traversal integration coverage.

## Related work

- Parent **AH-0MWL4SNKR001CDAA** — Procedurally generated Hex Map (epic).
- **AH-0MVXSHAS100010S0** — rush push into the next ring is playable (AC8 gap):
  the rush seam this item must not regress.
- **AH-0MWEZZ9TE001577J** — the ring-end hangar assault gate that runs before
  any advance.
- **AH-0MWHWF5D4000J0RB** — held-hex UPGRADE DEFENCES map action (blocked,
  tangential): consumes the map read model.

## Goal

Complete the content migration: remove the authored runtime table and the CSV
seeds, and move every scene, fixture, harness and test to the generator —
rings 1 and 2 now generate from the seed like every other ring.

**User story:** As a designer, I no longer author a table per ring; the
generator is the single content source and nothing can drift from it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The authored runtime table `HEX_RING_DEFINITIONS` and the `hex-ring-1.csv` / `hex-ring-2.csv` seeds are **retired as the runtime content source** (no scene or runtime path imports authored ring content; the CSV parity test is removed or replaced), and rings 1 and 2 generate from the seed like every other ring.
- `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts` is deleted or reduced to vocabulary re-exports only (no `HexRingDefinition` rows), `src/data/hex-ring-1.csv` / `hex-ring-2.csv` are deleted, and `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.test.ts` (the CSV parity test) is removed or replaced by a test that pins the generator as the single source.

- Fixtures and harnesses are migrated, not deleted where they still carry value: `src/core/hangarWar/__fixtures__/ringFixtures.ts`, `src/core/hangarWar/__fixtures__/aggressionScenarios.ts` and `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts` derive their sample rings from the generator for rings 1–3 (a deliberately pinned seed may replace hand-authored variety samples; any hand-authored fixture that no longer has a rationale is removed rather than left orphaned).

# Gym and game parity for generated rings

## Goal

Prove the gym and the game render and resolve exactly the same generated ring,
so the headless harness is trustworthy evidence for a seed-derived map.

**User story:** As a test/agent, `GymHexWar` renders the same generated model as
the game, so what I measure in the gym is what the player plays.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Unit, property and integration tests cover determinism, distinct-seed variety, invariant enforcement across many seeds and large ring indices, the grant-economy rule, and the save/load round-trip; `GymHexWar` renders the same generated model as the game.
- `GymHexWar` obtains its ring definitions from the same seed-aware source as the game (no gym-only authored fixture), and an explicit parity test asserts the gym and game read models are deep-equal for at least three seeds and ring indices 1, 2 and 3.
- `GymMiniBoss`'s HEX control resolves its deployment definition (the ring's weapon hex) from the generator for the payload's seed and ring index, so the boss body colour and opening volley come from the generated weapon hex rather than `hex-r1-6` fixture data.
- A parity assertion covers the intel read model (boss, strengths/weaknesses, aggression, grant) and the weapon-hex/special-mission flags, so a gym-only divergence fails loudly.
- `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`'s hex-ring rows are updated to describe the generated source and the new parity test as the evidence column (the docs sweep item may polish wording; this item's row must be accurate).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Notes & assumptions

- Parity means the same **pure read model**, not pixel equality: both sides call
  `buildHexMapModel` with definitions from the same source and the same payload.
- This item is the epic's gym↔game evidence gate; it must not introduce a
  gym-only code path to make the comparison pass.

**Key Files:**

- `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.ts` — the gym ring definitions source.

# Saved-build acceptance tests (red until implemented)

## Goal

Write the failing end-to-end acceptance tests that define *saved ship configurations* before any production code lands, so every later child turns an existing red test green (the same test-first pattern the parent used in AH-0MWL9E7PH001VPG5).

## Context

Parent: **AH-0MWL8C6FE008G1E7** — saved ship configurations (save / apply / rename / delete). The fired contract is: capture the currently equipped build, re-purchase + re-equip it in one action, refuse atomically with a structured shortfall, and preserve saved builds across a war reset.

Tests live beside the modules (repo convention) plus the scene-seam integration test:
- `src/core/hangarWar/savedBuild*.test.ts` (pure core: capture + apply + store round-trip)
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.test.ts` (payload parse/normalise additions)
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.savedBuild*.test.ts` (payload updaters + model rows)
- `src/scenes/hangarWarFlow.integration.test.ts` (scene seam: gym↔game parity through the shipped game config)

## Acceptance Criteria

- Red tests exist for **capture**: `buildFromHangar` records the equipped `activeHull`, the resolved starting weapons and modifiers, and the `weaponLevels`/`powerUpLevels` rows for exactly those kinds, and nothing else.
- Red tests exist for **affordable atomic apply**: every missing hull/weapon/modifier is purchased and equipped, every missing permanent level is bought, currency is spent exactly once, and the returned hangar is a fresh object with the input untouched.
- Red tests exist for **unaffordable refusal**: the structured shortfall names every missing entry/kind (and whether it is `gated`/`unknown`/`unaffordable`), reports exact minerals/cores, and asserts the returned hangar is byte-identical to the input (no spend, no partial purchase, no partial equip).
- Red tests exist for **stale build safety**: a saved build naming an id absent from the catalogue, or ring-gated under the current `ringIndex`, takes the refusal path (no throw, nothing applied) and respects the `owned → gated → unaffordable` precedence.
- Red tests exist for **payload round-trip**: `savedBuilds` is additive, absent in a legacy save, parsed when present, and omitted on write when empty (byte-for-byte round-trip, `HANGAR_WAR_VERSION` unchanged).
- Red tests exist for **management round-trip**: save → rename → delete of a saved build through the pure payload updaters, including that delete is reachable for every entry.
- Red tests exist for **war reset**: `restartHangarWar` keeps `savedBuilds` (and `bestScore`) while wiping unlocks, levels and loadout.
- Every test asserts a meaningful behaviour (no tautologies, no snapshot of internals); each fails for the documented reason before the implementation lands.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes — the saved-build tests are green in the full run executed through the test skill, whose dev-push gate enforces the suite.

- **Automated tests cover the feature through the pure core and the scene seam (gym↔game parity); the parent AC this child owns.** Saving captures the exact equipped set plus level rows; selecting an affordable build purchases and equips atomically; an unaffordable build reports every missing item/currency and applies nothing; rename/delete round-trip (deletion reachable for every saved build); a saved build missing a catalogue entry refuses safely; `restartHangarWar` keeps the saved-build list while wiping unlocks/levels/loadout; and the payload round-trips through `hangarWarStore` without a schema-version bump (the shape is additive).

## Minimal implementation

- Add the test files above with cases named after the parent's acceptance criteria.
- Use the existing fixtures (`src/core/hangarWar/fixtures.ts`, `createSampleHangarWarPayload`) and the deterministic seed/clock helpers rather than new bespoke fakes.
- Keep the pure-core tests catalogue-independent where possible by injecting a small catalogue, so they survive balance changes.

## Deliverables

- Failing tests in the four locations above, with a short header comment naming this item and the parent.
- A comment recording the red run (test names + failure reason per case).

## Dependencies

- None — this is the first child; every implementation child depends on it.

## Key Files

- `src/core/hangarWar/savedBuild.test.ts`
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.test.ts`
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.savedBuild.test.ts`
- `src/scenes/hangarWarFlow.integration.test.ts`
- `src/core/hangarWar/fixtures.ts`

## Notes

- Tests must be run through the test skill (`/skill:test`), never an ad-hoc `vitest` invocation.

# Saved-build contract and payload persistence

## Goal

Add the persisted saved-build contract — a `SavedShipBuild` row type and the additive `savedBuilds?` field on `HangarState` — parsed and normalised by the versioned store with **no schema-version bump**, following the established field-presence migration pattern (`weaponLevels`, `powerUpLevels`, `frontierTick`).

## Context

Parent: **AH-0MWL8C6FE008G1E7**. Design of record: `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D (persistence and save model). Today `HangarState` (`src/core/hangarWar/types.ts`) has no saved-build field, and `hangarWarStore.ts` normalises every hangar field through a per-field parser.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `SavedShipBuild` is defined in `src/core/hangarWar/types.ts` with: `id` (stable, rename-proof), `name` (display), `hullId`, `startingWeapons: string[]`, `modifiers: string[]`, and optional `weaponLevels` / `powerUpLevels` rows reusing `HangarWeaponLevelRow` / `HangarPowerUpLevelRow`.
- `HangarState.savedBuilds?: SavedShipBuild[]` is additive and optional, documented in the same style as `weaponLevels` (why additive, field-presence migration, omitted when empty).
- `parseHangarWarPayload` parses and normalises `savedBuilds`: unusable rows dropped (missing/blank/non-string `id` or `name`), names trimmed and length-bounded, whitespace-only names rejected, duplicate ids collapsed to the first mention, order preserved (no silent sorting).
- Stored ids are **not** catalogue-validated at parse time — a build naming an entry that no longer exists must survive the round-trip so apply can refuse safely (never silently shrink a build).
- Level rows inside a build are normalised through the economy's existing `normalisePermanentLevels`, so a hand-edited save cannot smuggle a non-upgradeable kind or an out-of-range level.
- A legacy save (no `savedBuilds`) parses with the field absent, and a hangar with an empty list writes **without** the field: the payload round-trips byte-for-byte and `HANGAR_WAR_VERSION` stays `1`.
- Unit tests cover every rule above (dropped rows, dedupe, trimming, level clamping, absent field, omitted-on-write).
- Module docblocks record the decision and link this item + the parent.

## Minimal implementation

- Add the `SavedShipBuild` interface and the optional hangar field in `types.ts`.
- Add a `parseSavedBuilds` normaliser in `hangarWarStore.ts` and call it from `parseHangar`; omit the field when empty.
- Extend `createSampleHangarWarPayload` (fixtures) with one sample saved build so the gym and integration tests exercise the new shape.
- Ensure `cloneHangar` / `withPermanentLevels` in `hangarEconomy.ts` carry `savedBuilds` through untouched (a clone must never drop a saved build).

## Deliverables

- Types, store parser and fixture updated with tests; no scene changes.

## Dependencies

- Depends on **Saved-build acceptance tests (red)** (this item's test child) — the red tests define the contract.

# Pure capture of the current ship build

## Goal

Add the pure helper that snapshots the currently equipped configuration as a `SavedShipBuild`, so "SAVE CURRENT BUILD" has no scene logic of its own and gym↔game parity holds.

## Context

Parent: **AH-0MWL8C6FE008G1E7**. The economy (`src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts`) already owns `resolveActiveHull`, `resolveActiveLoadout`, `hangarPermanentLevels` and `normalisePermanentLevels`; capture must compose them rather than re-derive the equipped set.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `buildFromHangar(hangar, name, id, catalogue?)` (naming free to adjust, signature documented) returns a `SavedShipBuild` capturing the **resolved** equipped state: `resolveActiveHull` for `hullId`, `resolveActiveLoadout(...).startingWeapons` and `.modifiers` for the loadout.
- Level rows are captured **only** for the build's own starting weapons and modifiers (never every owned kind), taken from `hangarPermanentLevels` and clamped/validated by `normalisePermanentLevels`; a kind with no bought row contributes no row.
- Name handling: trimmed, whitespace-only rejected (`null` return or a documented refusal), length-bounded by the same bound the store parser applies.
- `id` is a required input (the caller owns uniqueness) so the helper stays deterministic and side-effect-free — no clock, no randomness, no counter inside the economy.
- Pure and total: the input hangar is never mutated, the returned row is a detached copy, and a corrupt or empty hangar yields a valid starter build rather than throwing.
- Tests cover: full equipped build, empty loadout (AH-0MVZJ6V1J001DA9D legality), kinds with and without level rows, name trimming/rejection, and input immutability.

- **Save a named build (parent AC this child owns).** The hangar can capture the currently equipped ship configuration as a named saved build: the equipped hull (`activeHull`), the equipped starting weapons (`activeLoadout.startingWeapons`), the equipped modifiers (`activeLoadout.modifiers`), and the permanent levels that configuration relies on (`hangar.weaponLevels` / `hangar.powerUpLevels` rows for those kinds).

## Minimal implementation

- Implement the helper beside `equipLoadout` in `hangarEconomy.ts`.
- Reuse `resolveActiveHull` / `resolveActiveLoadout` / `hangarPermanentLevels` / `normalisePermanentLevels`.
- Add the name-bound constant once and share it with the store parser (single source).

## Deliverables

- Pure capture helper plus unit tests; no scene or store changes.

## Dependencies

- Depends on **Saved-build contract and payload persistence** (the row type it returns).

# Pure atomic apply of a saved build

## Goal

Add the pure reducer that re-purchases and re-equips a saved build in one action: it validates every part first, then applies purchase + equip + level upgrades atomically, or returns a structured shortfall and applies nothing.

## Context

Parent: **AH-0MWL8C6FE008G1E7**, hardest child. Existing primitives in `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts`: `canBuy`/`buy` (precedence `owned → gated → unaffordable`), `costToUpgrade`/`buyUpgrade` (one level per call, priced from the current level, capped at `MAX_PERMANENT_LEVEL`), `equipHull`, `equipLoadout`, `findHangarEntry`, `ownsEntry`. The sibling primitive AH-0MWL9EC3L002GKYR ("auto-enable a purchase") arms a *single* part; a build is many parts that must land together, so the atomicity stays in this reducer.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `applySavedBuild(hangar, build, context, catalogue?)` returns a discriminated result: `{ ok: true, hangar, spent }` or `{ ok: false, shortfall, hangar }` where the refused `hangar` is a detached copy of the input (nothing spent, nothing owned, nothing equipped differently).
- Parts are validated before any spend, using the existing `owned → gated → unaffordable` precedence per entry; a build whose hull/weapon/modifier is absent from the catalogue reports `unknown`, and one gated by `context.ringIndex` reports `gated`.
- Permanent levels are topped up to the captured level (never down): from the current level to the captured one, applying the same per-level curve `buyUpgrade` uses; a captured level above `MAX_PERMANENT_LEVEL` is clamped, and a captured level at or below the current level costs nothing.
- On success the hull becomes `activeHull`, the build's starting weapons and modifiers replace the active loadout exactly (through `equipHull`/`equipLoadout`), and the raised level rows are written through `withPermanentLevels`/`buyUpgrade` — spend, ownership, levels and equip all land in one returned hangar.
- The shortfall is structured and complete: the missing catalogue entries (id + kind + `gated`/`unknown`) **and** the exact aggregated mineral/core shortfall, computed over parts *and* level steps, so the UI can name what to earn.
- Atomicity is proven by test: an unaffordable build that would otherwise succeed on its first parts leaves currency, ownership, levels and loadout untouched; a build already fully owned and equipped is a no-op `ok` result that spends nothing.
- Duplicate ids inside a build, an empty name, and an empty loadout are handled without throwing.
- No scene, no persistence and no UI in this child — pure economy only, so gym↔game parity is automatic.

- **Affordable builds apply atomically; unaffordable builds report the shortfall (parent AC this child owns).** A build whose combined salvage cost the player cannot currently afford must report the exact shortfall (which entries, minerals and/or cores are missing) and apply **nothing** — neither partial purchase nor partial equip, and no currency spent.
- **A saved build referencing a now-unavailable entry never breaks (parent AC this child owns).** Selecting a saved build whose parts are not in the catalogue (or are ring-gated) reports the same shortfall/refusal path rather than throwing or silently applying a partial build; the economy's `owned → gated → unaffordable` precedence is respected.

## Minimal implementation

- Add the result/shortfall types and `applySavedBuild` beside `buy`/`buyUpgrade` in `hangarEconomy.ts`.
- Dry-run on a scratch hangar: apply `buy` per missing entry (with explicit equip at the end) and `buyUpgrade` per level step; if any step refuses, return the shortfall computed from the refusals and the untouched input.
- Aggregate prices with the existing `HangarPrice` shape; reuse `shortfallFor`-equivalent arithmetic already in the module rather than a second cost model.

## Deliverables

- Pure reducer + exhaustive unit tests (affordable, partially owned, unaffordable, gated, unknown, level top-up, already-satisfied no-op).

## Dependencies

- Depends on **Pure capture of the current ship build** (shares the row shape and the captured-levels semantics).
- Sequences after the per-part primitive AH-0MWL9EC3L002GKYR where it has landed; if it has not, this reducer owns purchase-plus-equip itself through `buy`/`equipHull`/`equipLoadout` and never a scene-only path.

# War reset preserves saved builds

## Goal

Make `restartHangarWar` keep the player's saved builds across a war reset, alongside `bestScore`, so re-saving a favourite build after every reset never happens (producer decision, 2026-11-17).

## Context

Parent: **AH-0MWL8C6FE008G1E7**. `restartHangarWar` (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts`) today returns `createDefaultPayload(seed)` with only `bestScore` carried across, which wipes the entire hangar including unlocks, levels and loadout. Saved builds are a "what you own / how you like to fly" meta-layer, so they survive; war progress does not.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `restartHangarWar(payload, seed)` returns a fresh payload whose `hangar.savedBuilds` equals the input's (deep-copied, so mutating the result can never mutate the input).
- The reset still wipes everything else: `unlockedHulls`/`unlockedWeapons`/`ownedModifiers` back to starters, `weaponLevels`/`powerUpLevels` removed, `activeLoadout` empty, salvage zero, ring back to `ringIndex` 1 with no hexes, `pendingAttacks` empty, `frontierTick` 0.
- `bestScore` and the fresh random seed behaviour are unchanged (no regression to AH-0MW8F7NH1002PQE3's documented reset contract).
- A payload with no saved builds resets exactly as today — no empty `savedBuilds: []` field appears (field-presence rule).
- The docblock on `restartHangarWar` records the saved-builds carry-over and cites this item + the producer decision.
- Unit tests assert each bullet above, including the remove-the-field-when-empty case.

## Minimal implementation

- Carry `savedBuilds` from `payload.hangar` onto `fresh.hangar` (deep copy) in `restartHangarWar`.
- Extend the existing restart tests in `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.test.ts` (or the saved-build test file) rather than creating a parallel suite.

## Deliverables

- Updated reset updater, updated docblock, extended tests.

## Dependencies

- Depends on **Saved-build contract and payload persistence** (the field it preserves).

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts` (`restartHangarWar`)
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts` (`createDefaultPayload`)
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.savedBuild.test.ts`

# Drop-down list of saved builds on the hangar screen

## Goal

Render the saved-build drop-down on the shared hangar screen model: one actionable row per saved build plus the save/manage entry rows, with scrolling when the list overflows, so both `HangarScene` and `GymHangar` show it from the same code.

## Context

Parent: **AH-0MWL8C6FE008G1E7**. The screen model (`buildHangarScreenModel` / `renderHangarScreen` in `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts`) already builds unlock rows, hull/weapon/modifier options, and the three bottom rows (`restart`/`map`/`deploy`) at pinned Y constants; `GymHangar` renders the same model read-only.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `HangarScreenModel` gains a saved-build section (rows plus the focused keys) that is **empty-friendly**: with no saved builds the screen shows a single muted `SAVE CURRENT BUILD` row (or the documented empty-state row) and nothing else changes.
- One actionable row per saved build, in payload order, activating that build (handler `onApplyBuild(buildId)`); each row shows the build name and its affordability cue (affordable vs shortfall) built from the pure economy/payload helpers, never recomputed in the renderer.
- Two fixed management rows: `SAVE CURRENT BUILD` (`onSaveBuild`) and `MANAGE BUILDS` (`onManageBuilds`). Both are omitted under `demo`, exactly like the restart row, so an attract run can never write a build.
- **Unbounded list, bounded screen:** the saved-build rows render inside a scrolling window (documented fixed visible-row count with a page/scroll step) so an arbitrarily long list never collides with the bottom rows; exported Y/layout constants pin the geometry and a layout test asserts no row overflows or overlaps `HANGAR_RESTART_ROW_Y`.
- `focusOrder` remains the single source of reading order: every actionable saved-build row is registered with the shared focus manager and no disabled row is focusable.
- Rendering a shortfall (unaffordable build) uses the same muted/refused styling as today's refused purchase rows and names what is missing at a readable width (truncation documented).
- `GymHangar` renders the same rows read-only (parity test), and `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` needs no exception.
- Pure model tests cover: empty list, one build, many builds with scrolling, affordability cue, demo omission, focus order, layout bounds.

- **One-action purchase and equip (parent AC this child owns).** A drop-down on the hangar screen lists saved builds; selecting one **purchases and equips every upgrade the build needs in one action** — the hull becomes `activeHull`, starting weapons join `activeLoadout.startingWeapons`, modifiers join `activeLoadout.modifiers`, and any missing permanent levels are bought — through the existing pure economy/payload updaters, never scene-only logic.

## Minimal implementation

- Extend `HangarScreenModel` and `buildHangarScreenModel` with the saved-build rows (built through a `buildSavedBuildRows` helper beside `buildHangarUnlockRows`).
- Add the scroll window as model data (visible slice + page hint), keeping the scene stateless about it beyond a scroll offset held like `restartArmed`.
- Extend `renderHangarScreen` to render the rows and wire the handlers (`onApplyBuild`, `onSaveBuild`, `onManageBuilds`).

## Deliverables

- Model + renderer extension, layout constants, model/render tests, `GymHangar` parity assertion.

## Dependencies

- Depends on **Saved-build contract and payload persistence**.

# Manage saved builds: rename mode and delete affordance

## Goal

Give every saved build a reachable rename and delete path through a manage mode on the same screen, so an unbounded list stays useful (producer decision: unbounded with a delete affordance).

## Context

Parent: **AH-0MWL8C6FE008G1E7**. The restart row already demonstrates the in-screen mode pattern: pure transition function (`advanceRestartConfirm`) plus scene-held state that survives every rebuild. Manage mode follows the same shape.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A pure mode model: `HangarScreenModel` can be built in `browse` or `manage` mode; `manage` mode presents exactly the focused/selected build with `RENAME`, `DELETE` (two-step confirm, mirroring the restart row) and `BACK` rows, and adding or removing builds never leaves a dangling selection.
- Pure payload updaters beside `purchaseHangarEntry`/`restartHangarWar`: `saveHangarBuild`, `renameHangarBuild`, `deleteHangarBuild`, each returning `{ ok, reason, payload }` style results with a fresh payload and a documented refusal vocabulary (e.g. `unknown` for an id not in the list, `invalid-name` for a blank/too-long name).
- `renameHangarBuild` keeps the build `id` stable and changes only the displayed name; `deleteHangarBuild` removes exactly one build and is reachable for **every** entry (a test enumerates the whole list and deletes each in turn).
- The delete confirm is two-step and times out like `advanceRestartConfirm`, exposed as a pure transition function so it is table-testable without a scene.
- Selection and mode state live in the scene (not the payload) and survive rebuilds, following the `restartArmed` precedent; leaving the screen returns to `browse`.
- Pure tests cover: browse/manage model contents, save/rename/delete round-trips, every-entry deletion, refusal cases, two-step confirm transitions, and that no updater mutates its input.
- No keystroke text entry in this child (rename is wired to the entry mode delivered by "Name entry keystroke mode for save and rename"); this child owns the model, updaters and confirm semantics.

- **Saved builds can be saved, renamed and deleted (parent AC this child owns).** The hangar surface supports creating a saved build from the current configuration, renaming an existing one, and deleting one, and the list is persisted in the hangar-war payload. **Saved builds survive a war reset** (producer decision): `restartHangarWar` preserves the saved-build list alongside `bestScore`, because saved configurations are a "what you own" meta-layer rather than war progress.
- **Saved builds are unbounded in number, with a delete affordance (parent AC this child owns).** There is no cap on how many saved builds a player may hold (producer decision), so the drop-down list plus the save/rename/delete surface is the only management mechanism — deleting a build must be reachable for every entry.

## Minimal implementation

- Add the mode to `HangarScreenModel` (additive field, defaulted to `browse`) and a `buildSavedBuildManageRows` helper.
- Add the three payload updaters in `hangarScreen.ts`, composing the pure build helpers (no economy arithmetic here).
- Add `advanceDeleteConfirm(armed, event)` beside `advanceRestartConfirm` and reuse its event union.

## Deliverables

- Model mode + manage rows, three payload updaters, confirm transition, tests.

## Dependencies

- Depends on **Drop-down list of saved builds on the hangar screen**.
- Rename completion depends on **Name entry keystroke mode for save and rename** (wired in "Wire saved builds into HangarScene with one persist").

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts` (model mode, payload updaters, confirm transition)
- `src/scenes/HangarScene.ts` (mode/selection state)
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHangar.ts` (read-only parity)

# Name entry keystroke mode for save and rename

## Goal

Add the keyboard text-entry mode the hangar screen needs to name a build — a pure buffer reducer plus the scene's key capture — so saving and renaming never require a prompt/overlay the game does not have.

## Context

Parent: **AH-0MWL8C6FE008G1E7**. The game is keyboard-driven and has no text-entry widget anywhere in `src/`; the hangar screen is a list of focusable rows rendered by `renderHangarScreen`, and `HangarScene` owns screen-level state. Rename therefore needs a small, testable edit mode rather than an OS prompt (which would break gym parity and the no-DOM-testability rule).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A pure reducer (e.g. `applyNameEdit(buffer, event)` where the event is `char` / `backspace` / `clear` / `commit` / `cancel`) owning: accepted character set (documented — letters, digits, space, hyphen, underscore), the maximum length shared with the store parser, and trimming on commit; the reducer is total and never mutates its input.
- Commit of a blank/whitespace-only name is refused with a documented reason instead of writing an empty name; cancel always restores the previous name.
- The edit mode is presented as a screen row (`SAVE CURRENT BUILD` / `RENAME` → edit row showing the buffer plus a caret and key hints) built in the model, so `GymHangar` still renders the same screen; nothing about the reducer depends on Phaser.
- `HangarScene` captures printable keys and Backspace only while in edit mode, and the mode leaks nothing: Esc/cancel restores browse mode, the restart confirm and edit mode can never be armed at the same time, and leaving the scene clears the mode.
- Entering edit mode for **save** prefills a deterministic default name (e.g. `BUILD <n>` derived from the current list length, or the hull name) and for **rename** prefills the current name — both asserted in tests.
- Pure tests cover the reducer (typing, max length, backspace at empty, cancel, commit trimming, invalid characters) and model tests cover the edit row; the scene key-capture path is covered through the scene seam test where a scene is already built.
- Documentation of the mode lives in the module docblock, linked to this item.

## Minimal implementation

- New pure module or `hangarScreen.ts` section for the buffer reducer (no Phaser import).
- Model rows for the edit mode plus `onNameEdit` handlers.
- Scene-level keyboard listener registered/unregistered with the mode, following the existing `FocusManager`/listener patterns.

## Deliverables

- Pure reducer + model rows + scene key capture + tests + docblock.

## Dependencies

- Depends on **Drop-down list of saved builds on the hangar screen**.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts` (buffer reducer, edit-mode rows)
- `src/scenes/HangarScene.ts` (key capture, mode state)
- `src/scenes/hangarWarFlow.integration.test.ts` (scene-seam coverage)

# Wire saved builds into HangarScene with one persist

## Goal

Wire apply / save / rename / delete through `HangarScene` so a save/rename/delete/apply each performs exactly one `saveHangarWarPayload` write, respects the demo guard, and restores focus across the rebuild.

## Context

Parent: **AH-0MWL8C6FE008G1E7**. `HangarScene` already has the established wiring shape: a public method per action (`buy`, `upgrade`, `equipHull`, `toggleWeapon`, `toggleModifier`, `restart`) that calls a pure updater, assigns `this.payload` on success, then `persist()` and `rebuildKeepingFocus(key)`. `persist()` is a no-op under demo, so demo/attract runs never overwrite the player's war.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `HangarScene` exposes `applySavedBuild(buildId)`, `saveBuild(name)`, `renameBuild(buildId, name)` and `deleteBuild(buildId)`, each returning a boolean ok flag, each calling the pure updater, and each performing at most one `persist()` call (asserted with an injected storage double counting `setItem`).
- A refused apply (unaffordable/gated/unknown) reports the shortfall on screen (a message row or the existing refused-purchase styling) and writes nothing: no currency change and **no storage write** at all.
- Focus is restored to the acted-on row after each rebuild (build row key for apply, the save row after save, the manage row after rename/delete), and a deleted build's row key falls back to the manage row rather than a dead key.
- Demo/attract runs: the saved-build rows are non-actionable, the attract decision function gains no saved-build branch, and no build action can reach `persist()`.
- The scene seam is covered end-to-end in `src/scenes/hangarWarFlow.integration.test.ts` under the shipped game config: save the current build, spend to change state, apply the build, and assert currency/ownership/loadout and the persisted payload.
- All four actions are exercised through the `GymHangar` parity surface or proven to be read-only there (no handler wiring), so gym↔game parity holds by construction.

## Minimal implementation

- Add the four public methods to `HangarScene`, mirroring the existing action methods.
- Extend `HangarScreenHandlers` with `onApplyBuild`, `onSaveBuild`, `onRenameBuild`, `onDeleteBuild`, `onManageBuilds`, `onNameEdit` and wire them in `build()`, omitting the mutating ones under `demo`.
- Route every write through the existing single `persist()`.

## Deliverables

- Scene wiring, handler extensions, persistence-count tests, integration test additions.

## Dependencies

- Depends on **Pure atomic apply of a saved build**, **Manage saved builds: rename mode and delete affordance** and **Name entry keystroke mode for save and rename**.
- Also needs **War reset preserves saved builds** landed so the reset path and the saved list agree.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/HangarScene.ts` (action methods, single persist, demo guard)
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts` (handler types, model rebuild, focus keys)
- `src/scenes/hangarWarFlow.integration.test.ts` (scene seam under the shipped config)

Part of `Review the per-deployment mineral income after pass-through collection (AH-0MWLCGXGW004KA3J)` — the verification/evidence slice, first in the plan's test-first ordering.

# Goal

As the producer, I want the **shipped** pass-through bot's income and movement churn measured from the actual shipped code, so the re-tune's recovery target and its anti-micro-positioning ceiling are pinned to evidence rather than to the stale committed artifact.

# Target outcome

A fresh harness run of the shipped bot (the pass-through change, commit `c2e3dadd`, on `origin/dev`) reproduces — or, where it does not, records — the post-pass-through baseline:

- ring 1 grind: **7.44** minerals/deployment at **44.4 %** capture (≈16.75 per captured);
- ring 2 grind: **2.67** minerals/deployment at **33.3 %** capture (≈8.0 per captured, the mini-boss checkpoint hold).

The same seeded runs record the movement-churn ceiling the re-tune must not exceed: turn-press count, turn duty cycle, forward-thrust toggles and reverse presses — with reverse presses on collection at/near zero.

# Definition of done

- `npm run ring-timing -- --one-level --income-out <scratch path>` runs against a tree containing `c2e3dadd` and its ring-1/ring-2 grind figures are recorded.
- The churn summary from `src/ai/eval/turnChurn.ts` is measured on the same seeded runs and recorded.
- Any deviation from the figures quoted in the parent item's "Existing state" is recorded with the actual measured value (the measurement is authoritative, not the quote).
- A comment on the parent records the measured income and churn baseline, with the command and the commit measured.

# Constraints

- **Read-only measurement.** No behavioural or tunable change in this item; it establishes the baseline the re-tune is judged against.
- **Measure the shipped tree.** The local `dev` checkout currently lags `origin/dev` (which carries `c2e3dadd`); measure from a tree that contains the pass-through commit.
- Do not overwrite `docs/dev/one-level-income-baseline.json` here — the regenerated artifact is the sibling item's deliverable.

# Risky assumptions

- The post-pass-through figures reproduce from the shipped bot. If they do not, the fresh measurement verdict stands and is recorded with the delta explained.

# Key Files

- `scripts/ring-timing.mjs` — the `--one-level --income-out` regeneration CLI.
- `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts` — the pure one-level income measurement core.
- `src/ai/eval/turnChurn.ts` — turn/churn metrics (turn presses, duty cycle, forward toggles, reverse presses).
- `src/ai/framework/competent/competentBot.integration.test.ts` — the seeded arena harness carrying the churn trace.
- `docs/dev/one-level-income-baseline.json` — the stale committed artifact (read-only reference).

# Acceptance Criteria

- A fresh `npm run ring-timing -- --one-level` run on the shipped bot (`c2e3dadd` or later) records ring-1 grind minerals/deployment, capture rate and minerals-per-captured, and the same three values for ring-2 grind.
- The measured churn baseline records turn-press count, turn duty cycle, forward-thrust toggles and reverse presses for the same seeded runs, and records reverse presses on collection (expected at/near zero).
- Every measured value that differs from the parent's quoted post-pass-through figures is stated with both the quoted and the measured value and a one-line explanation.
- A comment on the parent work item carries the measured income and churn baseline, the command used and the commit measured; it is reproducible from that comment.
- No source, tunable or committed artifact is modified by this item.

## Impact

The re-tune now starts from a measured, reproducible picture of what the shipped bot actually banks and how much it churns, so the recovery target and the movement ceiling are evidence rather than hearsay.

Part of `Review the per-deployment mineral income after pass-through collection (AH-0MWLCGXGW004KA3J)` — the test-first slice. It defines the re-tuned collection behaviour and the churn ceiling as tests **before** the implementation lands.

# Goal

As the producer, I want the "collect what it currently flies past, without precision braking" rule expressed as deterministic tests, so the re-tune cannot silently reintroduce thruster micro-positioning and the churn guard is in place before any behaviour changes.

# Target outcome

Deterministic, seeded tests that pin the desired end state:

- a mineral the shipped bot passes without collecting is collected on a pass-through route (intercept ahead / sweep the cluster / collect on the way through) — the exact route shape is the implementation sibling's choice, but the test asserts the mineral is banked;
- no retro-braking onto a pickup: `collectReverseBrake` stays off and reverse presses on collection stay at/near zero;
- the movement-churn regression gate is pinned to the sibling baseline item's measured ceiling: turn-press count, turn duty cycle, forward-thrust toggles and reverse presses at or below the shipped pass-through bot.

# Definition of done

- New tests in `src/ai/framework/competent/behaviours.test.ts` (and `goals.test.ts` where target selection is the seam) express route-through/cluster collection and the no-precision-braking rule.
- A churn regression test — in `competentBot.integration.test.ts` or `src/ai/eval/turnChurn.test.ts` — pins each churn metric to the measured baseline ceiling; each pin carries a comment naming the baseline source.
- The tests are added before the behaviour change and are expected to be red until the implementation sibling lands (or are written as a before/after discriminator that fails on the current bot and passes after).
- Each changed/added test assertion carries a comment stating why the expected value is the one it is.

# Constraints

- **Test-only slice.** No behaviour/tunable change here; the tests must be meaningful and deterministic on the seeded runs.
- Pins are the **measured** baseline from the sibling verification item, not invented numbers.
- Test scope follows `/skill:test`; do not run the full suite ad hoc.

# Risky assumptions

- The measured churn ceiling is stable enough across the three seeds to pin; if any metric is seed-noisy, pin it to the worst observed and record why.

# Key Files

- `src/ai/framework/competent/behaviours.test.ts` — collect behaviour unit tests.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/goals.test.ts` — target-selection / overshoot-filter unit tests.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/competentBot.integration.test.ts` — seeded arena churn trace.
- `src/ai/eval/turnChurn.ts` / `src/ai/eval/turnChurn.test.ts` — the churn summary.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/tunables.ts` — the `collectReverseBrake` / `collectOvershootMargin` knobs the tests exercise.

# Acceptance Criteria

- A deterministic test shows the re-tuned collection rule collects a mineral the current pass-through bot leaves behind, using a seeded fixture; the test is red on the shipped bot and green on the re-tuned bot.
- A test asserts collection never retro-brakes (`collectReverseBrake` false path) and that reverse presses on collection stay at/near zero on the seeded runs.
- A churn regression test asserts turn-press count, turn duty cycle, forward-thrust toggles and reverse presses are each at or below the measured shipped baseline, with a comment naming the baseline source.
- Every new/changed pin has a comment recording why that expected value was chosen.
- The changed-scope test gate (`/skill:test`) runs and the failures it reports are the expected red-before-green ones (or, if written as discriminators, the suite is green with the current bot recorded as the failing branch).

## Impact

The producer gets a machine-checked guarantee that recovering the minerals cannot come back as the thruster micro-positioning the pass-through change was asked to remove.

Measured recovery target (from the pre-pass-through baseline): ring-1 grind **9.0** minerals/deployment, ring-2 grind **6.0**, mini-boss checkpoint hold **18.0** per captured. Fallback, per the parent's AC: if the ceiling cannot be reached without a churn regression, the highest achieved figures are recorded, the guard is pinned to them, and the residual gap is filed as a linked balance item — the measured result stands.

# Speed Up power-up affects weapons only

## Problem statement

The Speed Boost (P5) power-up currently increases **both** the ship's movement speed (thrust and max speed) and its rate of fire by 50 % for 10 seconds. Design intent has changed: Speed Boost should be a **weapons-only** power-up — it must increase rate of fire but leave ship movement untouched. Today an active Speed Boost makes the ship harder to control (faster drift/top speed), which is not the intended effect.

## Users

- **Player** — when collecting a Speed Boost (P5), expects faster firing for the duration, with the ship handling exactly as normal.
  - *"As a player, when I collect a Speed Boost I want my weapons to fire faster, but my ship to handle exactly as it does without the power-up."*
- **Game designer / producer** — expects the GDD, power-up descriptions and README to describe P5 as a fire-rate boost only.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** — With P5 active, the player ship's **movement is unchanged**: thrust and max speed equal the un-boosted values in the playable game (`PlayScene`) and in every gym. `EffectsRegistry.speedMultiplier()` and `Player.setSpeedMultiplier()` no longer exist (removed, not left returning 1).
- **AC2** — With P5 active, the player's **rate of fire still increases by 50 %** (effective 1.5 × fire rate) for the level-resolved duration, applied live every frame through the single shared `CombatCoreScene._tickPlayer` step (so the game and all gyms inherit it); re-collect refreshes the full duration (never additive), expiry returns the rate to normal, and the boost survives respawn.
- **AC3** — `EffectsRegistry.fireRateMultiplier()` is the **single authority** for the P5 multiplier, reading the level-resolved catalogue stat directly (it no longer delegates to a removed movement accessor); the multiplier value and duration are unchanged.
- **AC4** — **Documentation updated:** the GDD P5 row says the Speed Boost increases **rate of fire** (not movement), and the `types.ts` description, `effects.ts`/`powerUpLevels.ts` doc comments/labels, README references and gym doc comments are updated to match. (CHANGELOG.md is excluded — managed by the ship skill release pipeline.)
- **AC5** — **Test cleanup and coverage:** existing tests that assert the P5 movement boost are removed/renamed (not silently left asserting removed behaviour); the fire-rate assertions are retained and strengthened; a regression test proves movement (thrust/max speed) is identical with P5 active while fire rate is boosted; parity/equivalence tests are updated to the new API.
- **AC6** — **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Impact

Speed Boost becomes a clean weapons-only power-up: players get faster fire without the ship suddenly handling differently, so the effect is predictable and no longer punishes movement control.

## Constraints

- P5 duration (level-resolved 10 s → 20 s) and multiplier value (1.5 × at level 0, cap 2.5 ×) must not change; only the movement axis is removed.
- The registry module must stay engine-agnostic (no Phaser imports).
- Gym parity principle: the game and every gym consume the same shared `_tickPlayer` step, so the change must not fork gym behaviour (`AGENTS.md` gym-parity rule).
- Hull run-stat speed scaling (`scaleShipConfigForHull`) is **not** part of P5 and must keep working — those deployments scale the base ship config, not `Player.setSpeedMultiplier`.
- No new balance config value is needed.

## Existing state

- `EffectsRegistry.speedMultiplier()` (`src/powerups/effects.ts`) returns the level-resolved `speed_boost` `speedMultiplier` stat (1.5 at level 0) while active, else 1.
- `EffectsRegistry.fireRateMultiplier()` currently simply returns `this.speedMultiplier()`.
- `CombatCoreScene._tickPlayer` (`src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`) applies both each frame:
  `player.setSpeedMultiplier(registry.speedMultiplier()); player.setFireRateMultiplier(registry.fireRateMultiplier());`
- `Player.setSpeedMultiplier()` (`src/entities/Player.ts`) stores `_speedMultiplier` and re-derives `_config` from `_baseConfig` via `_applySpeedMultiplier()`. It is called only from `_tickPlayer` (plus `setConfig` calls `_applySpeedMultiplier`).
- Hull speed scaling uses `scaleShipConfigForHull` (`src/core/hangarWar/hullSpeed.ts`), applied to the base `ShipConfig` at deployment — it does **not** call `Player.setSpeedMultiplier`.
- P5 is documented as movement + fire rate in: GDD §4.4 P5 row (`docs/Game Design Document.md` line ~1266), `src/powerups/types.ts` `speed_boost.description`, `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` label/rationale, `src/powerups/effects.ts` module doc, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.ts` module doc, README (shared combat core, effects registry, gym entries), and `src/scenes/gym/GymPlayer.ts` doc.
- Tests asserting the removed movement accessor (`EffectsRegistry.speedMultiplier()`): `src/powerups/effects.test.ts`, `src/powerups/__tests__/effects.permanent.test.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/__tests__/PlayScene.powerUpLevels.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/powerUpLeveling.parity.test.ts` (the `speed_boost: (r) => r.speedMultiplier()` probe map). Fire-rate-only assertions that must be kept and strengthened (they already call `fireRateMultiplier()`, so they need no accessor change): `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts`. No test calls `Player.setSpeedMultiplier()` directly (verified repo-wide), so no test needs updating for that removal.

## Desired change

1. **Remove** `EffectsRegistry.speedMultiplier()` and make `fireRateMultiplier()` read `stats('speed_boost').speedMultiplier ?? 1` directly while `speed_boost` is active (still a single authority for the fire-rate axis).
2. **Remove** the `player.setSpeedMultiplier(registry.speedMultiplier())` call from `CombatCoreScene._tickPlayer`, leaving only `setFireRateMultiplier(...)`.
3. **Remove** `Player.setSpeedMultiplier()` (and its now-dead `_speedMultiplier` / `_applySpeedMultiplier` support), folding the plain config assignment into `setConfig`; update the `Player._baseConfig` doc comment.
4. **Update docs/descriptions:** GDD P5 row, `types.ts` description, `powerUpLevels.ts` label/description/rationale, `effects.ts` module/roadmap comments, README references, `GymPowerUpsUtility`/`GymPlayer`/`hullSpeed`/`hangarDeployment` doc comments — all to describe P5 as a fire-rate (weapons-only) boost.
5. **Clean up tests:** delete/replace movement-boost assertions; keep and strengthen fire-rate assertions; add a regression test that movement (thrust/max speed) is identical with P5 active while fire rate is 1.5 ×.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — remove `speedMultiplier()`; have `fireRateMultiplier()` read the catalogue stat directly; update module doc.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — remove the `setSpeedMultiplier(...)` call from `_tickPlayer`; update the step doc/comment.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — remove `setSpeedMultiplier()` and its dead `_speedMultiplier`/`_applySpeedMultiplier` support; simplify `setConfig`; update `_baseConfig` doc.
- `src/powerups/types.ts` — change `speed_boost.description` to a rate-of-fire-only description.
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — update the `speed_boost` `speedMultiplier` spec label/description/rationale to fire-rate wording.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — update the P5 row and related references.
- `README.md` — update shared-core / effects-registry / gym references that mention movement + fire rate.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.ts` — update the module doc (Speed Boost bullet + `setSpeedMultiplier` reference).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPlayer.ts` — update the "live Speed Boost multipliers" doc wording.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hullSpeed.ts` — update the doc comment that references `Player.setSpeedMultiplier`.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.ts` — update the doc comment that references `Player.setSpeedMultiplier`.
- Tests: `src/powerups/effects.test.ts`, `src/powerups/__tests__/effects.permanent.test.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/__tests__/PlayScene.powerUpLevels.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/powerUpLeveling.parity.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts`.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUAYB9JS0025YUB** — "Speed power up should increase all speeds" (completed, shipped v0.1.6). This item **reverses** its movement-axis half: it added "all speeds" (movement + rate of fire); the new intent keeps only the weapon rate-of-fire half.
- **AH-0MU8QURXB008DWM7** — "PlayScene: apply P5 Speed Boost multiplier live" (completed). Added the original movement-only application; its movement half is now retired.
- **AH-0MTCNZX16007ECPS** — "Power-up catalogue + effects (P5, P8, P9)" (completed). Catalogue/effects foundation.
- **AH-0MTCNYWDO007B6CJ** — "Unit tests: power-up effects, refresh & magnet math" (completed). Test foundation to be cleaned up.
- **AH-0MVSTKGC3003OMAC** — "Temporary upgrades should always be temporary" (completed). Preserves re-collect/expiry semantics referenced by AC2.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MT97BW7M0056S8S** – Create gym scene with player ship and thrust-based space movement (completed)
- **AH-0MT9FS3DL0084Z6V** – Gym scene: ship config sliders, save button, half-speed ship (completed)
- **AH-0MUAYB9JS0025YUB** – Speed power up should increase all speeds (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: change, movement, powerup, ship, speed (+2 more)
- `README.md` — matched: change, movement, powerup, ship, speed (+2 more)
- `docs/BALANCING.md` — matched: affects, change, movement, powerup, ship (+2 more)

## Risks and assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk:** "weapons only" could be read to add other weapon effects (bullet speed, damage). Scope is bounded to **removing the movement-speed axis and keeping the existing fire-rate boost**; anything wider becomes a linked follow-up, not scope here.
- **API removal risk:** removing `EffectsRegistry.speedMultiplier()` / `Player.setSpeedMultiplier()` is a breaking internal API change. Mitigation: repo-wide search shows the only production caller is `_tickPlayer`; tests and doc comments are updated in the same change. `scaleShipConfigForHull` (hull run-stats) is independent and unaffected.
- **Misleading catalogue field name:** the level model stat is still called `speedMultiplier`. Renaming it to `fireRateMultiplier` would touch the power-up level specs, HUD and many tests; this item updates its user-facing label/description instead and leaves an internal rename to a potential follow-up.
- **Gym divergence risk:** gyms inherit `_tickPlayer`, so the removal must be made there only (never duplicated per-scene). Parity/equivalence tests are updated to guard this.
- **Assumption:** "Speed Up" in the item title refers to the existing **Speed Boost (P5)** power-up (no separate "Speed Up" power-up exists in the codebase).
- **Respawn interaction:** the multiplier must keep being re-applied each frame (fire-rate only) so it survives respawn and expiry — covered by AC2/AC5.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1: What is `EffectsRegistry.speedMultiplier()`?** — Answer (Map, research): It is the `effects.ts` method returning the Speed Boost (P5) movement-speed multiplier (level-resolved `speedMultiplier` stat, 1.5 at level 0, else 1). It feeds `Player.setSpeedMultiplier(...)` in `CombatCoreScene._tickPlayer`; `fireRateMultiplier()` currently delegates to it. Source: `src/powerups/effects.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`.
- **Q2: Should `EffectsRegistry.speedMultiplier()` be removed or kept?** — Answer (Producer, interactive reply, 2026-11-18): *"remove"*. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3: Should `Player.setSpeedMultiplier()` be removed?** — Answer (Producer, interactive reply, 2026-11-18): *"remove"*. Research: only `_tickPlayer` calls it; hull speed uses `scaleShipConfigForHull`. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q4: Should the GDD / descriptions / README be updated?** — Answer (Producer, interactive reply, 2026-11-18): *"yes"*. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q5: Should the existing movement-boost tests be updated?** — Answer (Producer, interactive reply, 2026-11-18): *"cleanup"*. Source: interactive reply.
